ranked_retrieved_results.content: ARIADNA EVALUATION REPORT V1.1 1. Status Version 1.1 supersedes report 1.0 and presents results obtained from the corrected split. The earlier report remains archived because it documents the leakage incident and supports reconstruction of decisions. Its metrics must not be used to compare systems. The official benchmark count is 2,302 semantic questions and 4,604 ES/EN records. The corpus freeze date is 31 May 2026. The pilot is planned for 15 September 2026. 2. Split correction Questions were grouped by semantic intent before assignment to a split. Every group contains translations, paraphrases, variants sharing the same answer, and cases sharing essential evidence. All group members remain together. Reconstruction produced 1,840 training semantic questions, 230 development questions, and 232 test questions. Spanish and English versions remain in the same split. Validation identifies zero orphaned pairs and zero divided groups. 3. Baselines BM25 achieves recall@10 of 0.69 and MRR of 0.52. The hybrid system achieves recall@10 of 0.80 and MRR of 0.63. The earlier value of 0.94 is identified as affected by leakage and is not an official result. Hybrid retrieval improves semantic, multi-hop, and temporal questions in particular. BM25 remains competitive for exact identifiers and low-ambiguity strings.

Reference answers contain expected facts, citations, acceptable alternative sources, relevant date, and non-answer conditions. ranked_retrieved_results.content: ARIADNA QUESTION ANNOTATION GUIDE V1.1 1. Purpose This guide defines how bilingual questions in the ARIADNA benchmark are created, classified, reviewed, and adjudicated. Version 1.1 incorporates revised criteria for temporal questions, multi-hop questions, version comparisons, and unanswerable cases following the reopening of the corpus. Every semantic question has one Spanish and one English version. Both share the intent, category, difficulty, reference answer, required facts, sources, citations, relevant date, and adjudication decision. Wording must be natural in each language and must not be a mechanical translation revealing answer terms. 2. Principles Questions must be answerable using the corpus alone. External knowledge, speculative inference, and subjective preference are not permitted. Difficulty must arise from locating, relating, and understanding evidence rather than deliberately confusing wording. A question remains grouped with its translations, paraphrases, and variants sharing an answer or essential evidence. This grouping prevents leakage across training, development, and test.

ranked_retrieved_results.content: ARIADNA BENCHMARK DESIGN AND CORPUS CONSTRUCTION PROTOCOL V1.0 1. Purpose ARIADNA is a bilingual benchmark for evaluating retrieval-augmented generation systems over administrative and scientific documentation from the NEXUS group. The benchmark studies whether a system retrieves relevant evidence, selects the correct temporal version, integrates distributed information, and produces an answer supported by verifiable citations. The corpus contains documents, emails, chats, notes, and events in Spanish and English. Every bilingual pair represents the same semantic content while using natural wording in each language. Conceptual identifiers, relations, and inclusion decisions must be equivalent across both versions. 2. Principles The design prioritizes traceability, temporal separation, reproducibility, difficulty diversity, and leakage prevention. A question cannot occur in a different partition from its translation, paraphrase, or variant sharing the same answer and evidence. Superseded documents are retained for historical questions, while questions about the current state must retrieve the current version. The benchmark distinguishes direct, temporal, multi-hop, version-comparison, and unanswerable questions. It also distinguishes easy, medium, and advanced difficulty. An unanswerable question must genuinely lack sufficient evidence; a retrieval failure does not turn an answerable question into an unanswerable one.

ranked_retrieved_results.content: ARIADNA EVALUATION REPORT V1.0 Document status This report records the first complete ARIADNA evaluation. After it was prepared, possible leakage across tuning and test splits was identified. Version 1.0 therefore remains archived and must not be used as the official performance reference. The original run reported recall@10 of 0.94 for the hybrid baseline. No model or index change justified such a large improvement over earlier results. Review found translations, paraphrases, and questions sharing an answer in different partitions. Original methodology The split was initially created by question identifier. This kept technical records separate but did not correctly group semantically equivalent intents. Spanish and English versions shared a parallel relation, although some additional reformulations were not connected. Consequence Question proximity allowed decisions made during tuning to directly benefit test cases. The value of 0.94 does not represent independent generalization. Run files are retained with an affected-result label to support auditing and reproduction of the incident. Incident record 1 Finding 1 affects separated ES/EN translations. Review uses automatic similarity and manual checking. Confirmed cases are grouped under one intent. The affected splits, experiments using the data, and potential effect on conclusions are recorded. The report does not delete the earlier result: it retains it with archived status and a visible explanation.

ranked_retrieved_results.content: ARIADNA FAITHFULNESS AND CITATION ERROR ANALYSIS REPORT V1.0 1. Summary This report analyzes 120 answers with citation and faithfulness problems. The sample contains direct, temporal, multi-hop, version-comparison, and unanswerable questions. The objective is to identify failure patterns and define post-generation controls. In forty-six answers, the citation supports part of the content but not an exception or condition. Thirty-one cite an earlier document version. In twenty-four, the correct evidence appears in a neighboring chunk that is not included. Nineteen answers combine two facts while providing one citation. 2. Method Every answer was decomposed into atomic claims. Reviewers checked the complete source, cited chunk, neighboring chunks, date, and version relations. Error type, severity, probable cause, and correction were recorded. An answer with correct content and incomplete evidence is not fully faithful. A citation pointing to the correct document but not allowing the relevant passage to be located receives partial credit for location rather than coverage. 3.

ranked_retrieved_results.content: ARIADNA RETRIEVAL BASELINE COMPARISON REPORT V1.0 1. Objective This report compares BM25, dense retrieval, and hybrid retrieval on the corrected ARIADNA split. Earlier results obtained from a split affected by leakage are retained only for auditing and are not used to compare systems. The main evaluation uses recall@10, MRR, latency, and analysis by category. Experiments use 256-token chunks, three seeds where applicable, and the corpus freeze date recorded in the manifest. 2. Systems BM25 serves as the lexical baseline and uses title, tags, and text. Dense retrieval uses a multilingual model. The hybrid system combines lexical and dense scores and applies lightweight reranking. Configurations share the same document collection and version filters. 3. Overall results BM25 achieves recall@10 of 0.69, MRR of 0.52, and median latency of 74 ms. Hybrid retrieval achieves recall@10 of 0.80, MRR of 0.63, and median latency of 182 ms. Improvement is concentrated in semantic, multi-hop, and temporal questions.

ranked_retrieved_results.content: ARIADNA USER EVALUATION AND CONSENT PROTOCOL V1.0 1. Purpose This protocol defines user evaluation of the ARIADNA system with staff from the Research Office at Sierra Centro Public University. It covers objectives, participants, recruitment, consent, tasks, metrics, collected data, security, retention, analysis, incidents, and closure. The study evaluates whether people can locate answers, interpret citations, distinguish current versions, understand abstention, and use language switching. It does not assess individual job performance or make decisions about participants. 2. Background A preliminary test with eight people produced thirty-seven comments. Three high-priority issues were identified: citation links did not always open the exact passage, answers did not clearly show when a policy was superseded, and the absence message did not distinguish missing evidence from retrieval failure. Priority corrections must be verified before the main evaluation. History and export functions are treated as future improvements rather than entry conditions. 3. Participants Recruitment targets twelve to sixteen Research Office staff with varied experience in projects, travel, policies, calls, and administration. Participation is voluntary.

ranked_retrieved_results.content: ARIADNA COMPLEX-CASE ADJUDICATION REGISTER V1.0 Purpose This register documents decisions on questions whose category, answer, date, difficulty, or evidence produced disagreement. Every case retains the initial labels, arguments, sources, final decision, and artifacts requiring updates. Procedure Two people review the case before the session. Adjudication consults the complete source rather than snippets alone. The person proposing the question may explain the intent but does not decide alone. The decision applies to the ES/EN pair. Session decisions Twelve cases were resolved. Four questions became temporal because the answer depended on a version valid on a specific date. Three became multi-hop because they required a relation among an event, task, and owner. Two became unanswerable because no explicit final date existed. Three were split or simplified because they contained two separate questions. Examples For a visit extension, a note explains the rationale, while a later email confirms the date. The answer must distinguish proposal from approval. For a pilot date, a provisional calendar cannot be treated as final without formal confirmation.

ranked_retrieved_results.content:
**Semantic-Cluster Summary**  
**Study Objectives and Scope**: Evaluates ARIADNA system usability for locating answers, interpreting citations, distinguishing current policy versions, and language switching. Does not assess job performance or make decisions about participants. Prior issues (e.g., citation link accuracy, superseded policy visibility) must be resolved before main evaluation.  

**Participants and Recruitment**: Targets 12–16 Research Office staff with varied experience; excludes those with potential coercion. Collects non-sensitive data (professional profile, search-system experience, starting language) for aggregated analysis. Participation is voluntary.  

**Consent and Ethics**: Requires ethics approval; prohibits recording free-text queries. Sessions use prepared tasks or interaction metrics. Participants may withdraw at any time.  

**Tasks and Procedures**:  
- **Task 1**: Locate current policy, verify non-superseded source using fictional benchmark artifacts.  
- **Task 2**: Answer temporal question using policy version valid on a stated date.  
- Tasks alternate order to reduce learning bias; removed if evidence/interface changes post-pilot.  

**Data Collection and Analysis**:  
- Metrics: Medians, percentages, distributions (not means alone).  
- Comments aggregated by theme, frequency, severity.  
- Links metrics to tasks/system versions; explains data exclusions.  

**Risks and Mitigations**:  
- **Risk 7 (Data Loss)**: Mitigated via clear instructions, session stop options, prepared tasks, restricted access.  
- **Risk 8 (Excessive Retention)**: Same mitigations as Risk 7.  
- Incidents trigger data protection and ethics lead notification.  

**Limitations**: Small groups interpreted cautiously; no causal conclusions drawn. Fictional artifacts used; no personal cases.

- **Projects & Frameworks**: SILEX (bilingual municipal systems dataset) includes 7 work packages, deliverables, SHACL validation, and risks (legal delays, data mapping gaps). ARIADNA evaluates systems via recall@10, hybrid models improve multi-hop queries but increase latency. Testing includes authentication, access control, and failure classification (blocking/major/minor).  
- **Governance & Controls**: Projects require version-controlled deliverables, legal confirmations, and data minimization policies. Controls (environment separation, logging) have owners, frequency, and evidence requirements; failures exclude datasets from products.

1. Purpose

ARIADNA is a bilingual benchmark for evaluating retrieval-augmented generation systems over administrative and scientific documentation from the NEXUS group. The benchmark studies whether a system retrieves relevant evidence, selects the correct temporal version, integrates distributed information, and produces an answer supported by verifiable citations.

The corpus contains documents, emails, chats, notes, and events in Spanish and English. Every bilingual pair represents the same semantic content while using natural wording in each language. Conceptual identifiers, relations, and inclusion decisions must be equivalent across both versions.

2. Principles

The design prioritizes traceability, temporal separation, reproducibility, difficulty diversity, and leakage prevention. A question cannot occur in a different partition from its translation, paraphrase, or variant sharing the same answer and evidence. Superseded documents are retained for historical questions, while questions about the current state must retrieve the current version.

The benchmark distinguishes direct, temporal, multi-hop, version-comparison, and unanswerable questions. It also distinguishes easy, medium, and advanced difficulty. An unanswerable question must genuinely lack sufficient evidence; a retrieval failure does not turn an answerable question into an unanswerable one.

3. Scope

The first official version contains 2,302 semantic questions and 4,604 language records. Every semantic question has one Spanish and one English version. The corpus uses artifacts from SILEX, LUMEN, VERDANT, ARIADNA, ORION, and LabOps. The source freeze date is recorded in the manifest.

Reference answers contain expected facts, citations, acceptable alternative sources, relevant date, and non-answer conditions. The benchmark does not require one exact wording, but every important claim must be covered by evidence.

Methodology section 1

Category 1, direct questions, is used where one source contains the main answer. Every question records its intent, difficulty, answer, required facts, sources, citations, and reference date. The annotator must justify why the category is appropriate and state discarded alternatives. ES/EN pairs share category, evidence, and decision even where wording is naturally adapted. Review checks that the question does not depend on external knowledge or an interpretation unsupported by the corpus.

Methodology section 2

Category 2, temporal questions, is used where the answer depends on date or validity. Every question records its intent, difficulty, answer, required facts, sources, citations, and reference date. The annotator must justify why the category is appropriate and state discarded alternatives. ES/EN pairs share category, evidence, and decision even where wording is naturally adapted. Review checks that the question does not depend on external knowledge or an interpretation unsupported by the corpus.

Methodology section 3

Category 3, multi-hop questions, is used where the answer combines two or more artifacts. Every question records its intent, difficulty, answer, required facts, sources, citations, and reference date. The annotator must justify why the category is appropriate and state discarded alternatives. ES/EN pairs share category, evidence, and decision even where wording is naturally adapted. Review checks that the question does not depend on external knowledge or an interpretation unsupported by the corpus.

Methodology section 4

Category 4, version comparison, is used where changes across documents must be distinguished. Every question records its intent, difficulty, answer, required facts, sources, citations, and reference date. The annotator must justify why the category is appropriate and state discarded alternatives. ES/EN pairs share category, evidence, and decision even where wording is naturally adapted. Review checks that the question does not depend on external knowledge or an interpretation unsupported by the corpus.

Methodology section 5

1. Purpose

ARIADNA is a bilingual benchmark for evaluating retrieval-augmented generation systems over administrative and scientific documentation from the NEXUS group. The benchmark studies whether a system retrieves relevant evidence, selects the correct temporal version, integrates distributed information, and produces an answer supported by verifiable citations.

The corpus contains documents, emails, chats, notes, and events in Spanish and English. Every bilingual pair represents the same semantic content while using natural wording in each language. Conceptual identifiers, relations, and inclusion decisions must be equivalent across both versions.

2. Principles

The design prioritizes traceability, temporal separation, reproducibility, difficulty diversity, and leakage prevention. A question cannot occur in a different partition from its translation, paraphrase, or variant sharing the same answer and evidence. Superseded documents are retained for historical questions, while questions about the current state must retrieve the current version.

The benchmark distinguishes direct, temporal, multi-hop, version-comparison, and unanswerable questions. It also distinguishes easy, medium, and advanced difficulty. An unanswerable question must genuinely lack sufficient evidence; a retrieval failure does not turn an answerable question into an unanswerable one.

3. Scope

The first official version contains 2,302 semantic questions and 4,604 language records. Every semantic question has one Spanish and one English version. The corpus uses artifacts from SILEX, LUMEN, VERDANT, ARIADNA, ORION, and LabOps. The source freeze date is recorded in the manifest.

Reference answers contain expected facts, citations, acceptable alternative sources, relevant date, and non-answer conditions. The benchmark does not require one exact wording, but every important claim must be covered by evidence.

Methodology section 1

Category 1, direct questions, is used where one source contains the main answer. Every question records its intent, difficulty, answer, required facts, sources, citations, and reference date. The annotator must justify why the category is appropriate and state discarded alternatives. ES/EN pairs share category, evidence, and decision even where wording is naturally adapted. Review checks that the question does not depend on external knowledge or an interpretation unsupported by the corpus.

Methodology section 2

Category 2, temporal questions, is used where the answer depends on date or validity. Every question records its intent, difficulty, answer, required facts, sources, citations, and reference date. The annotator must justify why the category is appropriate and state discarded alternatives. ES/EN pairs share category, evidence, and decision even where wording is naturally adapted. Review checks that the question does not depend on external knowledge or an interpretation unsupported by the corpus.

Methodology section 3

Category 3, multi-hop questions, is used where the answer combines two or more artifacts. Every question records its intent, difficulty, answer, required facts, sources, citations, and reference date. The annotator must justify why the category is appropriate and state discarded alternatives. ES/EN pairs share category, evidence, and decision even where wording is naturally adapted. Review checks that the question does not depend on external knowledge or an interpretation unsupported by the corpus.

Methodology section 4

Category 4, version comparison, is used where changes across documents must be distinguished. Every question records its intent, difficulty, answer, required facts, sources, citations, and reference date. The annotator must justify why the category is appropriate and state discarded alternatives. ES/EN pairs share category, evidence, and decision even where wording is naturally adapted. Review checks that the question does not depend on external knowledge or an interpretation unsupported by the corpus.

Methodology section 5

Source content: ORION FINAL REPORT AND REUSABLE DATA PACKAGE V1.0

1. Summary

ORION consolidated information about projects, publications, datasets, software, and research profiles within the NEXUS group. The final result is a reusable package with stable identifiers, verified relations, provenance, and sufficient documentation for controlled incorporation into ARIADNA and other internal systems.

The package does not reproduce every field from the original system. Internal metrics, audit records, personal addresses, review notes, and attributes without a clear purpose in the reusable product are excluded. Included fields retain their source system and extraction date.

2. Scope

The delivery contains tables for people, affiliations, projects, publications, datasets, software, organizations, and relations. It also includes identity tables, vocabularies, manifests, checksums, transformation rules, and an exclusion inventory.

Eight profiles remain outside the package because their identity could not be resolved with sufficient evidence. Fifteen historical records are retained as controlled distractors and explicitly marked as superseded versions or earlier states.

3. Principles

Reuse is based on traceability, minimization, version control, and separation between source and derived data. An inferred relation does not replace evidence. Profile merges require a recorded decision and retain earlier identifiers through equivalence relations.

Delivery section 1

Table 1, covering people, contains name, variants, identifiers, affiliations, and provenance. Every row uses a stable identifier and retains the source identifier where available. Normalized fields do not replace the original literal. Open, approximate, or pending dates are explicitly represented. The table includes cardinality and validation rules. Records failing criteria are isolated in a report and do not disappear from counts.

Delivery section 2

Normalized fields do not replace the original literal. Open, approximate, or pending dates are explicitly represented. The table includes cardinality and validation rules. Records failing criteria are isolated in a report and do not disappear from counts.

Records failing criteria are isolated in a report and do not disappear from counts.

Records failing criteria are isolated in a report and do not disappear from counts.

The annotator must justify why the category is appropriate and state discarded alternatives. ES/EN pairs share category, evidence, and decision even where wording is naturally adapted. Review checks that the question does not depend on external knowledge or an interpretation unsupported by the corpus.

Methodology section 2

Category 2, temporal questions, is used where the answer depends on date or validity. Every question records its intent, difficulty, answer, required facts, sources, citations, and reference date. The annotator must justify why the category is appropriate and state discarded alternatives. ES/EN pairs share category, evidence, and decision even where wording is naturally adapted. Review checks that the question does not depend on external knowledge or an interpretation unsupported by the corpus.

Methodology section 3

Category 3, multi-hop questions, is used where the answer combines two or more artifacts. Every question records its intent, difficulty, answer, required facts, sources, citations, and reference date. The annotator must justify why the category is appropriate and state discarded alternatives. ES/EN pairs share category, evidence, and decision even where wording is naturally adapted. Review checks that the question does not depend on external knowledge or an interpretation unsupported by the corpus.

Methodology section 4

Category 4, version comparison, is used where changes across documents must be distinguished. Every question records its intent, difficulty, answer, required facts, sources, citations, and reference date. The annotator must justify why the category is appropriate and state discarded alternatives. ES/EN pairs share category, evidence, and decision even where wording is naturally adapted. Review checks that the question does not depend on external knowledge or an interpretation unsupported by the corpus.

Claim: Improvement is concentrated in semantic, multi-hop, and temporal questions.
Source content: ARIADNA RETRIEVAL BASELINE COMPARISON REPORT V1.0

1. Objective

This report compares BM25, dense retrieval, and hybrid retrieval on the corrected ARIADNA split. Earlier results obtained from a split affected by leakage are retained only for auditing and are not used to compare systems.

The main evaluation uses recall@10, MRR, latency, and analysis by category. Experiments use 256-token chunks, three seeds where applicable, and the corpus freeze date recorded in the manifest.

2. Systems

BM25 serves as the lexical baseline and uses title, tags, and text. Dense retrieval uses a multilingual model. The hybrid system combines lexical and dense scores and applies lightweight reranking. Configurations share the same document collection and version filters.

3. Overall results

BM25 achieves recall@10 of 0.69, MRR of 0.52, and median latency of 74 ms. Hybrid retrieval achieves recall@10 of 0.80, MRR of 0.63, and median latency of 182 ms. Improvement is concentrated in semantic, multi-hop, and temporal questions. BM25 retains an advantage for exact identifiers and highly specific strings.

Detailed result 1

Analysis 1: direct questions. Results show that both systems retrieve sources containing explicit terms well. Recall, rank of the first relevant result, number of required sources, and latency are compared. Errors are manually reviewed to distinguish query, index, chunking, version, or relevance defects. Comparison uses confidence intervals and retains individual runs rather than the mean alone. A small difference is not presented as a definitive conclusion.

Detailed result 2

Analysis 2: temporal questions. Results show that hybrid retrieval finds related documents better but requires validity filters. Recall, rank of the first relevant result, number of required sources, and latency are compared. Errors are manually reviewed to distinguish query, index, chunking, version, or relevance defects. Comparison uses confidence intervals and retains individual runs rather than the mean alone. A small difference is not presented as a definitive conclusion.

Detailed result 3

Analysis 3: multi-hop questions. Results show that retrieval of complementary sources improves with dense signals. Recall, rank of the first relevant result, number of required sources, and latency are compared. Errors are manually reviewed to distinguish query, index, chunking, version, or relevance defects. Comparison uses confidence intervals and retains individual runs rather than the mean alone. A small difference is not presented as a definitive conclusion.

Detailed result 4

Analysis 4: version comparison. Results show that BM25 locates version numbers while hybrid retrieval broadens context. Recall, rank of the first relevant result, number of required sources, and latency are compared. Errors are manually reviewed to distinguish query, index, chunking, version, or relevance defects. Comparison uses confidence intervals and retains individual runs rather than the mean alone. A small difference is not presented as a definitive conclusion.

Detailed result 5

Analysis 5: unanswerable questions. Results show that no retriever should be treated as a perfect detector of absence. Recall, rank of the first relevant result, number of required sources, and latency are compared. Errors are manually reviewed to distinguish query, index, chunking, version, or relevance defects. Comparison uses confidence intervals and retains individual runs rather than the mean alone. A small difference is not presented as a definitive conclusion.

Detailed result 6

Experiment 1 compares C256 versus C512. The corpus, split, questions, and evaluation remain fixed. Any additional change is recorded as a separate factor. Results contain the exact configuration, seed, chunk count, and index checksum. Final selection considers effectiveness, operating cost, explainability, and cross-language stability. A configuration is not selected from one aggregate metric alone.

questions.question: Which offer was selected to expand Atlas-2's storage capacity?

gt_evidences.text: Offer B is selected for EUR 38,450, taxes included.

ranked_retrieved_results.content: ATLAS-2 STORAGE EXPANSION PROCUREMENT DECISION V1.0 Purpose This document records the comparison and purchasing decision for expansion of Atlas-2 storage. The need results from growth in ARIADNA corpora, LUMEN images, VERDANT products, and project working copies. Requirements The solution must provide at least 120 TB of usable capacity, tolerance of two disk failures, compatibility with the current system, monitoring, a five-year warranty, and delivery before 31 August 2026. The purchase includes disks, enclosures, controller, installation, and testing. Offers Three comparable offers were received. Offer A has the lowest price but only a three-year warranty. Offer B meets every requirement and includes installation and a recovery test. Offer C provides greater capacity but exceeds the available budget and has an incompatible delivery date. Decision Offer B is selected for EUR 38,450, taxes included. The decision is not based on price alone: it includes warranty, compatibility, support, delivery, and restoration evidence.

ranked_retrieved_results.content: ATLAS-2 MAINTENANCE AND CAPACITY UPGRADE REPORT V1.0 1. Summary The Atlas-2 maintenance window took place on 12 and 13 September 2026. It included storage expansion, updates to the base system, GPU drivers, the queue service, monitoring, and backup verification. Usable capacity increased from 84 TB to 196 TB. Twelve disks, two enclosures, and an additional controller were installed. The configuration tolerates two disk failures in every group. Read, write, simulated-failure, and restoration tests completed successfully. Service became available again on 13 September at 18:10. Two research jobs resumed from checkpoints, and one was rerun. No project information was lost. 2. Scope The intervention covered CPU nodes, three GPUs, working storage, archive storage, authentication, queues, monitoring, and backups. Access groups and quotas were not changed without a specific request. 3. Preparation Before the window, users were notified, new submissions stopped, backups verified, and active jobs recorded.

ranked_retrieved_results.content: ATLAS-2 OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE MANUAL V1.2 1. Purpose Atlas-2 is the shared computing and storage infrastructure of the NEXUS group. This manual defines daily operation, accounts, queues, storage, backups, maintenance, updates, monitoring, incidents, and recovery. The purpose is to provide reproducible capacity without compromising other projects or restricted data. The manual distinguishes administration, research use, and support. Users do not receive administrative permissions by default. Jobs must be identified, use persistent paths, and record the configuration required to reproduce results. 2. Components Atlas-2 includes CPU nodes, three GPUs, working storage, archival storage, a queue service, authentication, monitoring, and backups. Every component has an owner, version, dependencies, health check, and restoration procedure. 3. Principles Operation follows least privilege, project separation, quotas, traceability, and planned maintenance. Temporary jobs do not replace the archive. Restricted data is stored in separate directories with specific groups.

- **Projects & Frameworks**: SILEX (bilingual municipal systems dataset) includes 7 work packages, deliverables, SHACL validation, and risks (legal delays, data mapping gaps). ORION creates NEXUS entity data packages; ARIADNA benchmarks retrieval with 2,302 bilingual questions (recall@10: hybrid 0.80 vs. BM25 0.69). VERDANT ENERGY standardizes energy data (installations, quality codes).  
- **Ontologies & Data Models**: SILEX v1.1 uses language-independent identifiers and bilingual labels (`PublicService`). LUMEN defines archival terms (ES/EN); SolCentro specifies energy data fields.  
- **Validation & Testing**: SILEX Mapping Report resolved 63 violations (96.4% completeness) to 4 legal issues. ARIADNA evaluates systems via recall@10, hybrid models improve multi-hop queries but increase latency. Testing includes authentication, access control, and failure classification (blocking/major/minor).  
- **Governance & Controls**: Projects require version-controlled deliverables, legal confirmations, and data minimization policies. Controls (environment separation, logging) have owners, frequency, and evidence requirements; failures exclude datasets from products.  
- **Storage/Access Control**: Immutable storage, encryption, and retention policies; restricted spaces avoid personal sync. VERDANT API enforces policy checks, authentication, and 15-minute data restrictions.  
- **Risks & Limitations**: Risks include legal delays (SILEX), translation errors (LUMEN), and unresolved entity disambiguation (94% precision). Limitations: small sample sizes, multilingual model dependence (ARIADNA), incomplete documentation, and cross-system consistency issues (e.g., conflicting section numbering).  
- **Procurement/Maintenance**: Atlas-2 storage expansion prioritized Offer B (EUR 38,450, 120 TB, 5-year warranty). Maintenance includes firmware updates and post-upgrade verification (84 TB → 196 TB).  
- **Recruitment/Onboarding**: 12-month data engineer plan requires Python/SQL/version control; onboarding includes 1-week setup across ARIADNA/LUMEN/VERDANT systems.

Claim: The final package will contain an exclusion list with reasons so that absence of a dataset is not interpreted as an ingestion failure.
Source content: The person responsible for loading will check that the received file matches the authorization record. If additional fields appear, loading will stop until their treatment is confirmed. The manifest will record the result of this check, the file checksum, and any filtering performed before storage. Pending datasets will remain separate from authorized datasets so that an automated task cannot include them in a publication.

Annex B. Pre-publication review criteria

The pre-publication review must answer five questions: whether the dataset has a sufficient licence, whether it contains only necessary fields, whether versions and validity periods are correct, whether unnecessary personal data has been removed, and whether provenance explains every value. The answers must be documented by both a technical reviewer and a person responsible for licences or privacy.

Where a record combines sources with different conditions, the most restrictive condition will apply to the combined product unless the parts can be separated verifiably. Licence errors are blocking even where the record has passed technical tests. The final package will contain an exclusion list with reasons so that absence of a dataset is not interpreted as an ingestion failure.

1. Executive summary

The VERDANT pilot evaluated federated exchange of energy products among SolCentro, NEXUS, and Instituto Técnico do Norte. The architecture retained original fifteen-minute readings within SolCentro and delivered hourly or daily products subject to policy, purpose, minimum group size, and expiry.

The pilot processed data from sixty-two installations over eighty-nine days. Hourly products were generated where four valid intervals and at least three meters were available. Consumers received metadata, coverage, quality, and provenance together with the aggregate value.

All critical authentication, authorization, revocation, network, logging, and minimum-group tests passed. No exposure of individual readings, names, addresses, contracts, or secrets was identified. Product-request p95 latency was 1.68 seconds in the pre-production environment.

2. Objectives

Objectives were to demonstrate interoperability across connectors, enforce access policies, produce reproducible aggregates, preserve provenance, measure quality, and assess the usefulness of products for energy analysis.

Evaluation does not cover billing, automated installation control, or citizen use. Results apply to the versions, organizations, and period recorded in the manifest.

The project connects objects, people, places, dates, document types, events, and rights while retaining original description and uncertainty. ranked_retrieved_results.content: APPROXIMATE DATE AND HISTORICAL PLACE-NAME SCHEMA V0.8 This schema defines how non-exact dates and place names changing over time are represented. It does not replace archival description: source wording is retained and a structured interpretation is added for search. Every date contains `originalText`, `earliest`, `latest`, `precision`, and `interpretationSource`. An exact date uses the same value for earliest and latest. “1947” represents the complete year. “Spring 1947” retains the literal and uses a seasonal interval; it is not displayed as one day. “c. 1930” uses approximate precision. “Before 1952” has an upper bound and open beginning. The interface displays the original literal first. Calculated dates must not appear as transcriptions. Where two sources disagree, both assertions and their provenance are retained. Every place has a stable identifier. Names are stored with language, type, start, and end of use. A historical variant participates in search but leads to the same record. Namesake places must not be merged; disambiguation uses type, jurisdiction, collection, and related places. The system checks that earliest is not later than latest, every interpretation retains originalText, and precision belongs to the vocabulary. ES/EN pairs share identifiers and relations.

ranked_retrieved_results.content: LUMEN SECOND INGESTION AND DATA QUALITY REPORT V1.0 1. Summary The second LUMEN ingestion added 1,180 municipal correspondence letters and updated records from photography, posters, and person authorities. The batch was processed after applying terminology guide v1.1, the approximate-date schema, and corrections arising from the first linking evaluation. The run received 1,180 letter records and 1,164 digital files. Sixteen letters had no associated image but retained authorized metadata. The system processed every record and isolated errors without silently reducing counts. 2. Results Initial validation identified forty-seven non-normalized dates, twenty-nine ambiguous senders, eighteen place names without a sufficient candidate, twelve files with checksums differing from the manifest, and nine pending rights values. The twelve files were replaced with verified copies before processing continued. After correction, zero critical errors remained. Twenty-four person mentions remain unlinked, eleven places remain open, and nine objects remain outside the demonstrator because rights are pending. 3.

   - Answers must differentiate current states from unimplemented future changes.

ranked_retrieved_results.content: The LUMEN Rights and Reuse Protocol V1.0 defines classification modes (open, internal, restricted, pending) for metadata, images, and digital objects, with specific use permissions and controls. Objects are recorded with source, rights holder, conditions, and other metadata, assessed separately for original and digital rights. The demonstrator displays objects in full, as thumbnails, metadata-only, or excluded, without implying permission from file existence. Review processes involve classification by Mateo Ruiz Serra, archival context validation by Eva Calderón Gil, and licence review by Clara Ibáñez Soto. Uncertain cases remain pending until resolved. Controls emphasize using specific contractual/legal sources over internal notes, retaining historical versions when conditions change, generating public packages from approved lists with automated checks, and managing withdrawals with identifiers, reasons, dates, and verified deletions of caches/thumbnails.

1. Purpose

ARIADNA is a bilingual benchmark for evaluating retrieval-augmented generation systems over administrative and scientific documentation from the NEXUS group. The benchmark studies whether a system retrieves relevant evidence, selects the correct temporal version, integrates distributed information, and produces an answer supported by verifiable citations.

The corpus contains documents, emails, chats, notes, and events in Spanish and English. Every bilingual pair represents the same semantic content while using natural wording in each language. Conceptual identifiers, relations, and inclusion decisions must be equivalent across both versions.

2. Principles

The design prioritizes traceability, temporal separation, reproducibility, difficulty diversity, and leakage prevention. A question cannot occur in a different partition from its translation, paraphrase, or variant sharing the same answer and evidence. Superseded documents are retained for historical questions, while questions about the current state must retrieve the current version.

The benchmark distinguishes direct, temporal, multi-hop, version-comparison, and unanswerable questions. It also distinguishes easy, medium, and advanced difficulty. An unanswerable question must genuinely lack sufficient evidence; a retrieval failure does not turn an answerable question into an unanswerable one.

3. Scope

The first official version contains 2,302 semantic questions and 4,604 language records. Every semantic question has one Spanish and one English version. The corpus uses artifacts from SILEX, LUMEN, VERDANT, ARIADNA, ORION, and LabOps. The source freeze date is recorded in the manifest.

Reference answers contain expected facts, citations, acceptable alternative sources, relevant date, and non-answer conditions. The benchmark does not require one exact wording, but every important claim must be covered by evidence.

Methodology section 1

Category 1, direct questions, is used where one source contains the main answer. Every question records its intent, difficulty, answer, required facts, sources, citations, and reference date. Review checks that the question does not depend on external knowledge or an interpretation unsupported by the corpus.

questions.question: Is the claim that VERDANT centralizes original energy readings at NEXUS and that technical ability to query a product is equivalent to authorization supported?

gt_evidences.text: VERDANT studies interoperable exchange of energy products among SolCentro, Instituto Técnico do Norte, and NEXUS. The architecture is federated: original readings remain within the infrastructure of the partner generating them, while authorized consumers receive catalogues and derived products under explicit rules.

The design seeks interoperability, minimization, traceability, and revocation. Technical ability to query data is not authorization. Every product declares its purpose, owner, policy, version, provenance, and availability period.

The source retains authority over data. Federation exchanges descriptions and results and does not require centralized copies. Products may be withdrawn or superseded without losing history. Least privilege applies to accounts, networks, operations, and fields. Every transformation is reproducible, and logs contain no secrets or complete bodies.

ranked_retrieved_results.content: VERDANT PILOT FINAL REPORT V1.0 1. Executive summary The VERDANT pilot evaluated federated exchange of energy products among SolCentro, NEXUS, and Instituto Técnico do Norte. The architecture retained original fifteen-minute readings within SolCentro and delivered hourly or daily products subject to policy, purpose, minimum group size, and expiry. The pilot processed data from sixty-two installations over eighty-nine days. Hourly products were generated where four valid intervals and at least three meters were available. Consumers received metadata, coverage, quality, and provenance together with the aggregate value. All critical authentication, authorization, revocation, network, logging, and minimum-group tests passed. No exposure of individual readings, names, addresses, contracts, or secrets was identified. Product-request p95 latency was 1.68 seconds in the pre-production environment. 2. Objectives Objectives were to demonstrate interoperability across connectors, enforce access policies, produce reproducible aggregates, preserve provenance, measure quality, and assess the usefulness of products for energy analysis. Evaluation does not cover billing, automated installation control, or citizen use.

ranked_retrieved_results.content: VERDANT ENERGY READING SPECIFICATION V1.0 Purpose This specification defines the minimum profile for representing energy readings in the VERDANT pilot. It covers installations, meters, intervals, imported and exported energy, power, quality, time zone, and provenance. It does not itself authorize exchange: exportable products are determined by the privacy assessment. Identity The installation uses a stable identifier. The device identifier is retained for traceability but may change after replacement and must not function as the historical key. A meter replacement creates a new device entity linked to the same installation and its period of use. Time Every reading contains a start, end, duration, and time zone. The export uses local time with a UTC offset. Seasonal time changes must not produce unexplained duplicate or missing intervals. The operational interval is fifteen minutes, equivalent to ninety-six readings per complete day and meter. Measures and quality `importedEnergy` and `exportedEnergy` use kWh; `averagePower` uses kW. Contracted power provides context for outliers. Quality codes are measured, estimated, corrected, and missing. A null value without a code is an error.

Summary The security review assessed authentication, authorization, networking, certificates, secrets, logs, temporary storage, dependencies, administration, updates, and incident response for the VERDANT connector. Scope The SolCentro, NEXUS, and Instituto Técnico do Norte connectors were reviewed together with their integration and pre-production configurations, API schemas, and deployment procedures. Method The review combined configuration analysis, contract tests, negative tests, log inspection, dependency scanning, and configuration restoration. Every finding has a severity, asset, evidence, owner, date, and closure test. 4. Result No critical or high findings remain open. Two medium findings are temporarily accepted: manual rotation of one support credential and incomplete automation of an exception-expiry check. Both have an owner and date. Security result 1 Security domain 1 is authentication.

ranked_retrieved_results.content: VERDANT DATA QUALITY REPORT V1.0 1. Summary This report evaluates energy readings and derived products received during the VERDANT pilot. Evaluation covers temporal continuity, units, identifiers, quality codes, meter replacements, aggregation, coverage, and provenance. The main dataset contains sixty-two installations, sixty-four devices, and eighty-nine observation days. The difference between installations and devices results from two physical replacements. The system expected ninety-six fifteen-minute intervals per complete day and device, with documented adjustments for clock changes. 2. Overall results Measured readings cover 97.8% of expected intervals. Estimated readings account for 1.4%, corrected readings 0.3%, and records marked missing 0.5%. There are no null values without a quality code. The review identified thirty-one gap sequences, fourteen negative readings, nine unit changes, seven reused device identifiers, and four hourly products calculated with incomplete coverage. Every case was reviewed before final delivery. 3. Principles Quality is not summarized by one percentage. Every dimension has a rule, severity, exception, and evidence. An estimated value may be valid where declared. A measured reading may be incorrect where its unit or interval is inconsistent. 4. Method The pipeline compared manifests, profiled fields, validated schemas, checked continuity, calculated aggregates, and reviewed a sample. Corrections ran through versioned rules and retained the original value. Quality analysis 1 Dimension 1, completeness, covers expected, present, and missing intervals. The test records the field, rule, result, severity, and exception.

Resets and replacements are distinct events: resets retain devices with pre/post-values, while replacements close old periods and create new entities. Hourly products aggregate four intervals, declaring coverage and rule compliance. Export authorization depends on privacy assessments, not the specification itself. Repeated rules emphasize validation checks and event differentiation.

1. Executive summary

The VERDANT pilot evaluated federated exchange of energy products among SolCentro, NEXUS, and Instituto Técnico do Norte. The architecture retained original fifteen-minute readings within SolCentro and delivered hourly or daily products subject to policy, purpose, minimum group size, and expiry.

The pilot processed data from sixty-two installations over eighty-nine days. Hourly products were generated where four valid intervals and at least three meters were available. Consumers received metadata, coverage, quality, and provenance together with the aggregate value.

All critical authentication, authorization, revocation, network, logging, and minimum-group tests passed. No exposure of individual readings, names, addresses, contracts, or secrets was identified. Product-request p95 latency was 1.68 seconds in the pre-production environment.

2. Objectives

Objectives were to demonstrate interoperability across connectors, enforce access policies, produce reproducible aggregates, preserve provenance, measure quality, and assess the usefulness of products for energy analysis.

Evaluation does not cover billing, automated installation control, or citizen use. Results apply to the versions, organizations, and period recorded in the manifest.

Source content: VERDANT PILOT FINAL REPORT V1.0

1. Executive summary

The VERDANT pilot evaluated federated exchange of energy products among SolCentro, NEXUS, and Instituto Técnico do Norte. The architecture retained original fifteen-minute readings within SolCentro and delivered hourly or daily products subject to policy, purpose, minimum group size, and expiry.

The pilot processed data from sixty-two installations over eighty-nine days. Hourly products were generated where four valid intervals and at least three meters were available. Consumers received metadata, coverage, quality, and provenance together with the aggregate value.

All critical authentication, authorization, revocation, network, logging, and minimum-group tests passed. No exposure of individual readings, names, addresses, contracts, or secrets was identified. Product-request p95 latency was 1.68 seconds in the pre-production environment.

2. Objectives

Objectives were to demonstrate interoperability across connectors, enforce access policies, produce reproducible aggregates, preserve provenance, measure quality, and assess the usefulness of products for energy analysis.

Evaluation does not cover billing, automated installation control, or citizen use. Results apply to the versions, organizations, and period recorded in the manifest.

3. Governance

Andrés Beltrán Vega led VERDANT. Inés Ferrer Lozano maintained the model and quality. Sergio Vidal Cruz managed storage and pipelines. Nuria Castaño Rey coordinated infrastructure. Héctor Molina Frías reviewed privacy and security. Carmen Rey represented SolCentro. Bruno Almeida coordinated Instituto Técnico do Norte.

Decisions were recorded with their purpose, alternatives, owner, date, and artifacts. Exceptions had an expiry. Proposals were not treated as approved until confirmation was received.

raw.source_content:
VERDANT PILOT FINAL REPORT V1.0

1. Executive summary

The VERDANT pilot evaluated federated exchange of energy products among SolCentro, NEXUS, and Instituto Técnico do Norte. The architecture retained original fifteen-minute readings within SolCentro and delivered hourly or daily products subject to policy, purpose, minimum group size, and expiry.

The pilot processed data from sixty-two installations over eighty-nine days. Hourly products were generated where four valid intervals and at least three meters were available. Consumers received metadata, coverage, quality, and provenance together with the aggregate value.

All critical authentication, authorization, revocation, network, logging, and minimum-group tests passed. No exposure of individual readings, names, addresses, contracts, or secrets was identified. Product-request p95 latency was 1.68 seconds in the pre-production environment.

2. Objectives

Objectives were to demonstrate interoperability across connectors, enforce access policies, produce reproducible aggregates, preserve provenance, measure quality, and assess the usefulness of products for energy analysis.

Evaluation does not cover billing, automated installation control, or citizen use. Results apply to the versions, organizations, and period recorded in the manifest.

3. Governance

Andrés Beltrán Vega led VERDANT. Inés Ferrer Lozano maintained the model and quality. Sergio Vidal Cruz managed storage and pipelines. Nuria Castaño Rey coordinated infrastructure. Héctor Molina Frías reviewed privacy and security. Carmen Rey represented SolCentro. Bruno Almeida coordinated Instituto Técnico do Norte.

Claim: Registration data will remain outside the public pilot and will be used in internal tests only where written authorization exists.
Source content: Every load will have a manifest, checksum, date, licence, source system, and owner. Transformations will preserve the original value where normalization changes its form. Corrected errors will remain linked to the earlier version for auditing.

6. Validation and acceptance

Validation will combine schema checks, SHACL shapes, regression tests, and manual review. Minimum criteria are zero duplicate identifiers, zero critical errors, complete language labels, at least 95% completeness for mandatory fields, and ES/EN result equivalence of at least 98%. Accepted warnings must correspond to known exceptions.

The API must respond in less than two seconds at the 95th percentile for the agreed queries. Users will complete six tasks. A defect is considered blocking if it prevents discovery of a procedure, displays an incorrect deadline, loses context when language changes, or exposes unauthorized data.

7. Communication and change control

Formal communications will use email and remain linked to the corresponding document or decision. Chats support coordination but do not replace approval. Changes to scope, date, licence, or acceptance criteria require a request containing reason, impact, alternatives, and owners.

The current plan will remain available when a revision is published. A new version will state which sections changed and from what date they apply. History will not be rewritten to make a provisional proposal appear to have been approved from the beginning.

R1. Incomplete mappings

Fields without a responsible unit or legal basis may prevent transformation. Mitigation consists of requesting a new export, explicitly marking pending values, and not inferring information absent from an authorized source.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

R2. Duplicate identifiers

Reuse of local codes may cause collisions. Identifiers will combine the source system, procedure type, and local number, and a regression test will prevent recurrence.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

R3. Registration-data licence

Lack of formal confirmation limits scope. Registration data will remain outside the public pilot and will be used in internal tests only where written authorization exists.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

R4. Bilingual inconsistency

Divergent labels or messages may produce different results. Every class, property, status, and API message will be reviewed in parallel and use a shared language-independent identifier.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

R5. Environment delay

Unavailability of municipal infrastructure may shorten testing. An equivalent UPSC environment will be retained, but final acceptance requires repeating checks on the municipal network.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

R6. SHACL false positives

Overly general rules may flag informational procedures as errors. Shapes will be conditional on procedure type, and accepted warnings will include justification.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

R7. Pilot-date change

ranked_retrieved_results.content: ARIADNA RETRIEVAL BASELINE COMPARISON REPORT V1.0 1. Objective This report compares BM25, dense retrieval, and hybrid retrieval on the corrected ARIADNA split. Earlier results obtained from a split affected by leakage are retained only for auditing and are not used to compare systems. The main evaluation uses recall@10, MRR, latency, and analysis by category. Experiments use 256-token chunks, three seeds where applicable, and the corpus freeze date recorded in the manifest. 2. Systems BM25 serves as the lexical baseline and uses title, tags, and text. Dense retrieval uses a multilingual model. The hybrid system combines lexical and dense scores and applies lightweight reranking. Configurations share the same document collection and version filters. 3. Overall results BM25 achieves recall@10 of 0.69, MRR of 0.52, and median latency of 74 ms. Hybrid retrieval achieves recall@10 of 0.80, MRR of 0.63, and median latency of 182 ms. Improvement is concentrated in semantic, multi-hop, and temporal questions.

ranked_retrieved_results.content: ARIADNA BENCHMARK DESIGN AND CORPUS CONSTRUCTION PROTOCOL V1.0 1. Purpose ARIADNA is a bilingual benchmark for evaluating retrieval-augmented generation systems over administrative and scientific documentation from the NEXUS group. The benchmark studies whether a system retrieves relevant evidence, selects the correct temporal version, integrates distributed information, and produces an answer supported by verifiable citations. The corpus contains documents, emails, chats, notes, and events in Spanish and English. Every bilingual pair represents the same semantic content while using natural wording in each language. Conceptual identifiers, relations, and inclusion decisions must be equivalent across both versions. 2. Principles The design prioritizes traceability, temporal separation, reproducibility, difficulty diversity, and leakage prevention. A question cannot occur in a different partition from its translation, paraphrase, or variant sharing the same answer and evidence. Superseded documents are retained for historical questions, while questions about the current state must retrieve the current version. The benchmark distinguishes direct, temporal, multi-hop, version-comparison, and unanswerable questions. It also distinguishes easy, medium, and advanced difficulty. An unanswerable question must genuinely lack sufficient evidence; a retrieval failure does not turn an answerable question into an unanswerable one.

ranked_retrieved_results.content: The ARIADNA evaluation rubric assesses answers using seven dimensions: faithfulness (claims supported by evidence), completeness (presence of required elements), relevance (focus on the question), temporal accuracy (date-appropriate facts), citation coverage (locatable evidence for all claims), abstention quality (avoiding invented answers for unanswerable questions), and bilingual consistency (equivalent facts in ES/EN). Each dimension uses a 0–1 scale with qualitative labels, requiring evaluators to record numerators, denominators, scores, and explanations. Claims and expected elements are evaluated separately; unsupported or irrelevant claims reduce faithfulness/relevance. Disagreements are resolved using answers, questions, reference records, and complete sources. Examples illustrate scenarios like faithful but incomplete answers, complete but unfaithful answers, and appropriate abstention. Calibration involves adjudicated examples, with evaluators required to reach minimum agreement before scoring.

**4. Methodology**: Direct questions (Category 1) rely on single-source answers. Each question documents intent, difficulty, required facts, sources, and citations. Annotators justify category assignments and discarded alternatives. Spanish/English pairs share semantic structure, evidence, and decisions despite natural wording differences. Reviews ensure no external knowledge or unsupported interpretations.

Claim: The final result is a reusable package with stable identifiers, verified relations, provenance, and sufficient documentation for controlled incorporation into ARIADNA and other internal systems.
Source content: ORION FINAL REPORT AND REUSABLE DATA PACKAGE V1.0

1. Summary

ORION consolidated information about projects, publications, datasets, software, and research profiles within the NEXUS group. The final result is a reusable package with stable identifiers, verified relations, provenance, and sufficient documentation for controlled incorporation into ARIADNA and other internal systems.

The package does not reproduce every field from the original system. Internal metrics, audit records, personal addresses, review notes, and attributes without a clear purpose in the reusable product are excluded. Included fields retain their source system and extraction date.

2. Scope

The delivery contains tables for people, affiliations, projects, publications, datasets, software, organizations, and relations. It also includes identity tables, vocabularies, manifests, checksums, transformation rules, and an exclusion inventory.

Eight profiles remain outside the package because their identity could not be resolved with sufficient evidence. Fifteen historical records are retained as controlled distractors and explicitly marked as superseded versions or earlier states.

3. Principles

Reuse is based on traceability, minimization, version control, and separation between source and derived data. An inferred relation does not replace evidence. Profile merges require a recorded decision and retain earlier identifiers through equivalence relations.

Delivery section 1

Table 1, covering people, contains name, variants, identifiers, affiliations, and provenance. Every row uses a stable identifier and retains the source identifier where available. Normalized fields do not replace the original literal. Open, approximate, or pending dates are explicitly represented. The table includes cardinality and validation rules. Records failing criteria are isolated in a report and do not disappear from counts.

Delivery section 2

Records failing criteria are isolated in a report and do not disappear from counts.

questions.question: Synthesize how the SILEX municipal pilot was prepared, deployed, and evaluated, including the schedule change, deployment conditions, main results, and evaluation limitations.

gt_evidences.text: The pilot originally planned for September is delayed by three dependencies: confirmation of pending fields in the municipal export, configuration of the pre-production network, and final review of API messages. The new operating window is set from 5 to 16 October 2026. The date is treated as approved following joint confirmation by NEXUS and the Santa Marina City Council.

SILEX demonstrates that a heterogeneous municipal catalogue can be transformed into an interoperable, bilingual, and verifiable semantic representation. The pilot covers the catalogue, ontology, mappings, API, deployment, training, evaluation with municipal staff, transfer, and closure.

SILEX was deployed in the Santa Marina City Council pre-production environment after network configuration, named accounts, secrets, and API contract tests were completed. This report documents infrastructure, versions, steps, incidents, results, and rollback.

The first planned window was postponed because authorized network addresses and two municipal accounts were missing. The executed window took place on 21 and 22 September 2026. The environment became available for training and internal tests before the pilot began in October.

The candidate load contains authorized procedures, vocabularies, units, legal bases, and version relations. The municipal register and other restricted datasets remain outside. The load retains a manifest, source, licence, and counts.

The overall success rate was 88%. Median task time was 2 minutes 18 seconds. Language switching preserved the query and entity in 100% of journeys. The API achieved p95 latency of 1.42 seconds during sessions. No exposure of restricted data was identified.
The evaluation does not measure large-scale citizen use and does not replace a complete accessibility audit. Results apply to the environment, corpus, and versions recorded in the manifest.

Purpose and scope This plan defines the organization of the SILEX pilot phase, whose purpose is to determine whether a heterogeneous municipal catalogue can be transformed into an interoperable, bilingual, and verifiable semantic representation. The pilot is jointly conducted by the NEXUS group at Sierra Centro Public University and the Santa Marina City Council. Its scope covers procedure selection, field mapping, ontology publication, data validation, API deployment, and evaluation with municipal staff. The plan does not itself authorize reuse of every available dataset. Each source retains its own licence and access conditions. In particular, the municipal register of residents is treated as restricted until the municipal legal office confirms permitted uses in writing. Technical availability of an export will not be interpreted as authorization to publish or redistribute it. Version 1.0 uses 15 September 2026 as the reference date for the start of the pilot. If mappings, licences, or the environment make that date infeasible, project management will prepare a change proposal. An alternative date remains provisional until formally approved by the steering committee and confirmed in writing by the municipality.

ranked_retrieved_results.content: Conclusion SILEX can proceed without using personal content from the municipal register. The core of the pilot is based on administrative metadata and interoperability rules. Legal uncertainty must appear as an explicit restriction rather than be hidden by a technical decision. Publication of the catalogue and final transfer require evidence of licence, provenance, validation, and access control. Formal confirmation from Santa Marina will be the determining document for any use of registration data beyond a limited internal test. Annex A. Evidence required to authorize a load Before a municipal dataset is loaded, the authorization record must precisely identify the source system, included fields, purpose, people with access, and destination environment. It must state whether authorization covers a copy, remote consultation, or synthetic data only. It must also set a review date and explain what will happen when the pilot ends. A generic reference to the project does not replace this information. The person responsible for loading will check that the received file matches the authorization record. If additional fields appear, loading will stop until their treatment is confirmed. The manifest will record the result of this check, the file checksum, and any filtering performed before storage. Pending datasets will remain separate from authorized datasets so that an automated task cannot include them in a publication. Annex B. Pre-publication review criteria The pre-publication review must answer five questions: whether the dataset has a sufficient licence, whether it contains only necessary fields, whether versions and validity periods are correct, whether unnecessary personal data has been removed, and whether provenance explains every value. The answers must be documented by both a technical reviewer and a person responsible for licences or privacy. Where a record combines sources with different conditions, the most restrictive condition will apply to the combined product unless the parts can be separated verifiably. Licence errors are blocking even where the record has passed technical tests. The final package will contain an exclusion list with reasons so that absence of a dataset is not interpreted as an ingestion failure.

ranked_retrieved_results.content: 4. Specific assessment of registration data The municipal register supports proof of residence and contains personal information. The SILEX catalogue does not need to copy individual records. It is sufficient to describe the registration-certificate procedure, requirements, unit, channel, and deadline. The preferred option is therefore to exclude register content from the semantic product. If an internal test needs to check a connection to the system, it must use a controlled environment, a minimum sample, or synthetic data. Access will be limited to designated people, logs will not retain complete bodies, and the test will have an end date. Authorization must state whether a copy may be moved or only the municipal system may be queried. Until the legal office issues formal confirmation, the dataset will be classified as restricted and awaiting a licence. This classification does not prevent the rest of the pilot from proceeding. The plan and deliverable must state that registration data is outside the public scope. 5. Metadata and legal bases Procedure metadata may be published where it is public administrative information and contains no unnecessary personal data.

ranked_retrieved_results.content: SILEX PILOT FINAL EVALUATION REPORT V1.0 1. Executive summary The final SILEX pilot evaluation was conducted with ten participants from the Santa Marina City Council between 7 and 14 October 2026. Participants represented citizen services, urban planning, trade, environment, the general secretariat, and electronic administration. Every participant completed six procedure-search and review tasks followed by a questionnaire and short interview. Evaluation measured success, time, requests for help, clarity, ease of search, ES/EN consistency, and confidence in deadlines and legal bases. The overall success rate was 88%. Median task time was 2 minutes 18 seconds. Language switching preserved the query and entity in 100% of journeys. The API achieved p95 latency of 1.42 seconds during sessions. No exposure of restricted data was identified. 2. Scope Tasks covered locating a procedure, identifying the competent unit, checking a channel, interpreting a deadline, comparing a legal version, and switching language. Authorized procedures and data without personal cases were used. The evaluation does not measure large-scale citizen use and does not replace a complete accessibility audit. Results apply to the environment, corpus, and versions recorded in the manifest.

It incorporates responses from the Santa Marina City Council, licence conditions for the exports, and decisions concerning demonstration, transfer, and retention. The main conclusion is that SILEX may publish procedure metadata and use synthetic records or authorized samples in internal tests. Personal content from the municipal register is not part of the open catalogue or general transfer package. 2. Information categories Procedure metadata, case data, personal data from the register, technical identifiers, audit records, and project documentation are distinguished. Every category has a purpose, access level, retention period, and permitted products. Titles, descriptions, units, channels, deadlines, and legal bases may be added to the catalogue where their source and conditions permit. Personal contact names are excluded unless expressly required. 3. Municipal register The registration-certificate procedure may be described without copying individual records. Any connection test uses synthetic data or a minimum sample in a restricted environment. Authorization for an internal test is not a redistribution licence. 4.

ranked_retrieved_results.content: PRELIMINARY LEGAL ASSESSMENT FOR REUSE OF MUNICIPAL DATA This document analyzes the initial conditions for using Santa Marina City Council data and metadata in the SILEX project. It does not replace a decision by the legal office and does not itself grant authorization. Its purpose is to identify pending decisions, minimum controls, and limits that must be reflected in planning, architecture, and publication. The assessment distinguishes procedure metadata, case data, and personal data from the municipal register. These categories do not have the same risk or basis of use. It also distinguishes internal access, demonstration to selected users, transfer between organizations, and open publication. 1. Context SILEX needs procedure information to construct mappings, validate the ontology, and test an API. Most fields are administrative descriptions: titles, units, channels, deadlines, and legal bases. However, some exports may contain contact names, technical identifiers, or references to individual cases. The existence of a copy in a municipal system does not imply that it may be transferred to the university. Before a dataset is received, the decision maker, purpose, licence or authorization, fields, and retention period must be identified. Restrictions must travel with the data and appear in the manifest.

ranked_retrieved_results.content: 2. Delivery principles SILEX follows five principles. First, values will not be invented to fill missing data. Second, every change will be traceable to a source, responsible person, and date. Third, the Spanish and English versions will share identifiers and meaning. Fourth, validation will occur before publication or deployment. Fifth, legal and organizational decisions take precedence over technical availability. Data will be classified as present, missing, non-applicable, excluded, or awaiting validation. This distinction is mandatory because it affects SHACL rules, interface presentation, and metric interpretation. An empty field alone is not sufficient to express its status. 3. Governance Javier Ortega Campos acts as scientific lead and contact point with Santa Marina. Luis Noguera coordinates municipal staff and validates local names, units, and processes. Mireia Soler Pons leads ontology work; Alba Prieto Mora maintains the catalogue and test data; Nuria Castaño Rey manages deployment and security; Sergio Vidal Cruz administers storage, ingestion, and backups; Clara Ibáñez Soto coordinates budget, evidence, and closure. The steering committee will meet monthly and whenever a critical blocker arises. Decisions will be classified as approved, provisional, or rejected.

ranked_retrieved_results.content: DELIVERABLE D3 — SILEX MAPPING AND VALIDATION REPORT This report documents the method used to transform the municipal catalogue into the SILEX ontology, the batch 3 validation results, agreed corrections, and criteria for accepting the candidate version. It retains both initial and post-correction results so the effect of every change can be verified. Batch 3 contains 412 records. The first run produced sixty-three violations across forty-one records: twenty-eight missing competent units, seventeen non-normalized dates, eleven duplicate identifiers, and seven statuses outside the vocabulary. Nine channel warnings were also identified as false positives. 1. Sources and scope Sources are the revised Santa Marina catalogue, ontology specification v1.1, auxiliary unit and legal-basis tables, and status and channel vocabularies. Validation does not include individual cases or registration-data content. Personal examples used during development are synthetic. Mapping covers identifiers, titles, descriptions, units, legal bases, channels, deadlines, statuses, provenance, and version relations. Local presentation fields are excluded where they add no interoperable meaning. Every exclusion includes its reason and source system.

**Cluster 1: Project Scope & Governance**  
- SILEX pilot aims to transform a municipal dataset into an interoperable, bilingual, verifiable semantic representation.  
- Jointly conducted by NEXUS group (Sierra Centro Public University) and Santa Marina City Council.  
- Scope: procedure selection, ontology publication, API deployment, validation, and staff evaluation.
