ranked_retrieved_results.content: VERDANT DATA GOVERNANCE AND ACCESS POLICY V1.0 Purpose This policy defines who may discover, request, generate, receive, and retain VERDANT products. It applies to SolCentro, NEXUS, and Instituto Técnico do Norte during the pilot and transfer. Principles The source retains authority over data. Minimization, specific purpose, least privilege, traceability, expiry, and revocation apply. Fifteen-minute data remains at SolCentro. External products are hourly or daily and require at least three meters. Roles The data owner approves purpose and products. The data steward maintains the catalogue, quality, and policies. The connector operator administers the service. The consumer requests products. The security reviewer verifies controls. The auditor reads evidence without changing data. Decisions Every product has an identifier, purpose, schema, frequency, minimum group, owner, policy, version, and review date. An exception has a scope and expiry. Absence of a response is not interpreted as approval. Access Policy evaluates identity, role, product, operation, purpose, period, and environment. A valid credential is insufficient by itself. The administration endpoint is limited to authorized networks. Retention Products have a retention period. Temporary copies are deleted, and deletion is verified. Audit records are retained for thirty days and contain no complete bodies.

ORION creates NEXUS entity data packages; ARIADNA benchmarks retrieval with 2,302 bilingual questions (recall@10: hybrid 0.80 vs. BM25 0.69). VERDANT ENERGY standardizes energy data (installations, quality codes).  
- **Ontologies & Data Models**: SILEX v1.1 uses language-independent identifiers and bilingual labels (`PublicService`). LUMEN defines archival terms (ES/EN); SolCentro specifies energy data fields.

ARIADNA evaluates systems via recall@10, hybrid models improve multi-hop queries but increase latency. Testing includes authentication, access control, and failure classification (blocking/major/minor).  
- **Governance & Controls**: Projects require version-controlled deliverables, legal confirmations, and data minimization policies. Controls (environment separation, logging) have owners, frequency, and evidence requirements; failures exclude datasets from products.  
- **Storage/Access Control**: Immutable storage, encryption, and retention policies; restricted spaces avoid personal sync. VERDANT API enforces policy checks, authentication, and 15-minute data restrictions.  
- **Risks & Limitations**: Risks include legal delays (SILEX), translation errors (LUMEN), and unresolved entity disambiguation (94% precision). Source content: Every load will have a manifest, checksum, date, licence, source system, and owner. Transformations will preserve the original value where normalization changes its form. Corrected errors will remain linked to the earlier version for auditing.

6. Validation and acceptance

Validation will combine schema checks, SHACL shapes, regression tests, and manual review. Minimum criteria are zero duplicate identifiers, zero critical errors, complete language labels, at least 95% completeness for mandatory fields, and ES/EN result equivalence of at least 98%. Accepted warnings must correspond to known exceptions.

The API must respond in less than two seconds at the 95th percentile for the agreed queries. Users will complete six tasks. A defect is considered blocking if it prevents discovery of a procedure, displays an incorrect deadline, loses context when language changes, or exposes unauthorized data.

7. Communication and change control

Formal communications will use email and remain linked to the corresponding document or decision. Chats support coordination but do not replace approval. Changes to scope, date, licence, or acceptance criteria require a request containing reason, impact, alternatives, and owners.

The current plan will remain available when a revision is published. A new version will state which sections changed and from what date they apply. History will not be rewritten to make a provisional proposal appear to have been approved from the beginning.

R1. Incomplete mappings

Fields without a responsible unit or legal basis may prevent transformation. Mitigation consists of requesting a new export, explicitly marking pending values, and not inferring information absent from an authorized source.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

R2. Duplicate identifiers

Reuse of local codes may cause collisions. Identifiers will combine the source system, procedure type, and local number, and a regression test will prevent recurrence.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

R3. Registration-data licence

Lack of formal confirmation limits scope. Registration data will remain outside the public pilot and will be used in internal tests only where written authorization exists.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

R4. Bilingual inconsistency

Divergent labels or messages may produce different results. Every class, property, status, and API message will be reviewed in parallel and use a shared language-independent identifier.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

R5. Environment delay

Unavailability of municipal infrastructure may shorten testing. An equivalent UPSC environment will be retained, but final acceptance requires repeating checks on the municipal network.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

R6. SHACL false positives

Overly general rules may flag informational procedures as errors. Shapes will be conditional on procedure type, and accepted warnings will include justification.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

R7. Pilot-date change

ORION consolidated information about projects, publications, datasets, software, and research profiles within the NEXUS group. The final result is a reusable package with stable identifiers, verified relations, provenance, and sufficient documentation for controlled incorporation into ARIADNA and other internal systems.

The package does not reproduce every field from the original system. Internal metrics, audit records, personal addresses, review notes, and attributes without a clear purpose in the reusable product are excluded. Included fields retain their source system and extraction date.

Claim: Registration data will remain outside the public pilot and will be used in internal tests only where written authorization exists.
Source content: Every load will have a manifest, checksum, date, licence, source system, and owner. Transformations will preserve the original value where normalization changes its form. Corrected errors will remain linked to the earlier version for auditing.

6. Validation and acceptance

Validation will combine schema checks, SHACL shapes, regression tests, and manual review. Minimum criteria are zero duplicate identifiers, zero critical errors, complete language labels, at least 95% completeness for mandatory fields, and ES/EN result equivalence of at least 98%. Accepted warnings must correspond to known exceptions.

The API must respond in less than two seconds at the 95th percentile for the agreed queries. Users will complete six tasks. A defect is considered blocking if it prevents discovery of a procedure, displays an incorrect deadline, loses context when language changes, or exposes unauthorized data.

7. Communication and change control

Formal communications will use email and remain linked to the corresponding document or decision. Chats support coordination but do not replace approval. Changes to scope, date, licence, or acceptance criteria require a request containing reason, impact, alternatives, and owners.

The current plan will remain available when a revision is published. A new version will state which sections changed and from what date they apply. History will not be rewritten to make a provisional proposal appear to have been approved from the beginning.

R1. Incomplete mappings

Fields without a responsible unit or legal basis may prevent transformation. Mitigation consists of requesting a new export, explicitly marking pending values, and not inferring information absent from an authorized source.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

R2. Duplicate identifiers

Reuse of local codes may cause collisions. Identifiers will combine the source system, procedure type, and local number, and a regression test will prevent recurrence.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

R3. Registration-data licence

Lack of formal confirmation limits scope. Registration data will remain outside the public pilot and will be used in internal tests only where written authorization exists.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

R4. Bilingual inconsistency

Divergent labels or messages may produce different results. Every class, property, status, and API message will be reviewed in parallel and use a shared language-independent identifier.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

R5. Environment delay

Unavailability of municipal infrastructure may shorten testing. An equivalent UPSC environment will be retained, but final acceptance requires repeating checks on the municipal network.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

R6. SHACL false positives

Overly general rules may flag informational procedures as errors. Shapes will be conditional on procedure type, and accepted warnings will include justification.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

R7. Pilot-date change

Claim: Licence errors are blocking even where the record has passed technical tests.
Source content: The person responsible for loading will check that the received file matches the authorization record. If additional fields appear, loading will stop until their treatment is confirmed. The manifest will record the result of this check, the file checksum, and any filtering performed before storage. Pending datasets will remain separate from authorized datasets so that an automated task cannot include them in a publication.

Annex B. Pre-publication review criteria

The pre-publication review must answer five questions: whether the dataset has a sufficient licence, whether it contains only necessary fields, whether versions and validity periods are correct, whether unnecessary personal data has been removed, and whether provenance explains every value. The answers must be documented by both a technical reviewer and a person responsible for licences or privacy.

Where a record combines sources with different conditions, the most restrictive condition will apply to the combined product unless the parts can be separated verifiably. Licence errors are blocking even where the record has passed technical tests. The final package will contain an exclusion list with reasons so that absence of a dataset is not interpreted as an ingestion failure.

questions.question: What must the team do if a failure occurs during Atlas-2 maintenance, and which checks must be completed before declaring the service operational?

gt_evidences.text: Maintenance step 1 is to prepare the window and notify. The record identifies the time, person, command or tool, result, and evidence. Where a failure appears, the team decides whether to continue, isolate the component, or roll back. The service is not declared operational until authentication, storage, CPU and GPU submission, monitoring, and restoration are complete. ranked_retrieved_results.content: ATLAS-2 OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE MANUAL V1.2 1. Purpose Atlas-2 is the shared computing and storage infrastructure of the NEXUS group. This manual defines daily operation, accounts, queues, storage, backups, maintenance, updates, monitoring, incidents, and recovery. The purpose is to provide reproducible capacity without compromising other projects or restricted data. The manual distinguishes administration, research use, and support. Users do not receive administrative permissions by default. Jobs must be identified, use persistent paths, and record the configuration required to reproduce results. 2. Components Atlas-2 includes CPU nodes, three GPUs, working storage, archival storage, a queue service, authentication, monitoring, and backups. Every component has an owner, version, dependencies, health check, and restoration procedure. 3. Principles Operation follows least privilege, project separation, quotas, traceability, and planned maintenance. Temporary jobs do not replace the archive. Restricted data is stored in separate directories with specific groups.

ranked_retrieved_results.content: ATLAS-2 MAINTENANCE AND CAPACITY UPGRADE REPORT V1.0 1. Summary The Atlas-2 maintenance window took place on 12 and 13 September 2026. It included storage expansion, updates to the base system, GPU drivers, the queue service, monitoring, and backup verification. Usable capacity increased from 84 TB to 196 TB. Twelve disks, two enclosures, and an additional controller were installed. The configuration tolerates two disk failures in every group. Read, write, simulated-failure, and restoration tests completed successfully. Service became available again on 13 September at 18:10. Two research jobs resumed from checkpoints, and one was rerun. No project information was lost. 2. Scope The intervention covered CPU nodes, three GPUs, working storage, archive storage, authentication, queues, monitoring, and backups. Access groups and quotas were not changed without a specific request. 3. Preparation Before the window, users were notified, new submissions stopped, backups verified, and active jobs recorded.

The need results from growth in ARIADNA corpora, LUMEN images, VERDANT products, and project working copies. Requirements The solution must provide at least 120 TB of usable capacity, tolerance of two disk failures, compatibility with the current system, monitoring, a five-year warranty, and delivery before 31 August 2026. The purchase includes disks, enclosures, controller, installation, and testing. Offers Three comparable offers were received. Offer A has the lowest price but only a three-year warranty. Offer B meets every requirement and includes installation and a recovery test. Offer C provides greater capacity but exceeds the available budget and has an incompatible delivery date. Decision Offer B is selected for EUR 38,450, taxes included. The decision is not based on price alone: it includes warranty, compatibility, support, delivery, and restoration evidence.

6. Validation and acceptance

Validation will combine schema checks, SHACL shapes, regression tests, and manual review. Minimum criteria are zero duplicate identifiers, zero critical errors, complete language labels, at least 95% completeness for mandatory fields, and ES/EN result equivalence of at least 98%. Accepted warnings must correspond to known exceptions.

The API must respond in less than two seconds at the 95th percentile for the agreed queries. Users will complete six tasks. A defect is considered blocking if it prevents discovery of a procedure, displays an incorrect deadline, loses context when language changes, or exposes unauthorized data.

7. Communication and change control

Formal communications will use email and remain linked to the corresponding document or decision. Chats support coordination but do not replace approval. Changes to scope, date, licence, or acceptance criteria require a request containing reason, impact, alternatives, and owners.

The current plan will remain available when a revision is published. A new version will state which sections changed and from what date they apply. History will not be rewritten to make a provisional proposal appear to have been approved from the beginning.

R1. Incomplete mappings

Fields without a responsible unit or legal basis may prevent transformation. Mitigation consists of requesting a new export, explicitly marking pending values, and not inferring information absent from an authorized source.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

R2. Duplicate identifiers

Reuse of local codes may cause collisions. Identifiers will combine the source system, procedure type, and local number, and a regression test will prevent recurrence.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

R3. Registration-data licence

Lack of formal confirmation limits scope. Registration data will remain outside the public pilot and will be used in internal tests only where written authorization exists.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

R4. Bilingual inconsistency

Divergent labels or messages may produce different results. Every class, property, status, and API message will be reviewed in parallel and use a shared language-independent identifier.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

R5. Environment delay

Unavailability of municipal infrastructure may shorten testing. An equivalent UPSC environment will be retained, but final acceptance requires repeating checks on the municipal network.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

R6. SHACL false positives

Overly general rules may flag informational procedures as errors. Shapes will be conditional on procedure type, and accepted warnings will include justification.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

R7. Pilot-date change

Source content: Every case was assigned an owner and target date. The correction must preserve evidence of the previous value and run through the pipeline. Where a correction changes meaning, review by the municipal owner is required.

5. Duplicate-identifier incident

Identifier SM-LIC-042 was used for both a terrace and a market stall because two municipal applications shared numbering. Loading stopped before resources were overwritten. The solution combines system, domain, and local number: SM-URBAN-TERRACE-042 and SM-MARKET-STALL-042.

The regression test searches for repetition within the batch, across previous loads, and among different types. It also verifies that references to documents and units are updated with the new identifier. The old source code is retained as an alternative identifier with provenance.

6. SHACL-shape adjustments

The channel shape required at least one value for every record. This was incorrect for purely informational records. The new rule applies cardinality only to procedures that accept an application or provide an operational service. Informational records may declare the field non-applicable.

The date rule is extended to accept a year, interval, or exact date but not free text without an assessment. Bilingual labels are checked by base identifier. The version shape prevents cycles and requires reciprocity between previous and next versions.

7. Regression set

The set contains twenty-four procedures not used during diagnosis: six permits, five certificates, four grants, four prior notifications, and five informational records. It checks the identifier, unit, legal basis, channel, deadline, status, and labels.

It contains two non-applicable cases and three pending fields to prevent corrections from turning explicit states into gaps. The expected result is zero duplicates and zero labels without a language. A recurring failure blocks publication of ontology v1.2.

8. Post-correction results

The second run reduced critical violations to four records with legal bases awaiting municipal validation. These cases will not be published as complete and will retain the pending assessment. Duplicates, date formats, and unmapped statuses were corrected.

The nine channel warnings disappeared after the rule became conditional. Comparison of reports confirms that no correction removed original information. ES/EN label coverage reached 100% in the batch, and completeness of publishable mandatory fields was 96.4%.

9. Risks and schedule

Validation depends on Santa Marina confirming the four pending legal bases. Schedule risk remains open: if confirmation arrives after August, the final load and pilot must be rescheduled. An alternative date will not be treated as approved until formal communication is received.

The deliverable must clearly distinguish the plan date from a change proposal. Metrics, annexes, and examples will be reviewed in both the editable source and PDF. Required signatures are those of Javier Ortega Campos and Luis Noguera.

10. Conclusions

The approach transforms the catalogue without hiding uncertainty. Separating missing, non-applicable, excluded, and pending values was essential to avoid false errors and complete the model without inventing data. Compound identifiers remove collisions, and regression tests reduce the risk of recurrence.

The candidate version may proceed to pre-production once municipal confirmations are incorporated, full validation is repeated, and the signed report is archived. Registration data remains outside the publishable scope until a sufficient formal licence exists.

Annex A. Minimum evidence per record

Every publishable record must include an identified source, extraction date, licence, owner, validation result, and relation to its previous version where applicable. Transformed values must retain the source field. Isolated manual corrections are not accepted.

Annex B. Rerun procedure

The rerun starts from a clean copy, installs the exact ontology and shape versions, loads the manifest, transforms the records, executes the rules, and generates two outputs: a readable report and a structured file. Checksums are compared before approval.

The second run reduced critical violations to four records with legal bases awaiting municipal validation. These cases will not be published as complete and will retain the pending assessment. Duplicates, date formats, and unmapped statuses were corrected.

The nine channel warnings disappeared after the rule became conditional. Comparison of reports confirms that no correction removed original information. ES/EN label coverage reached 100% in the batch, and completeness of publishable mandatory fields was 96.4%.

9. Risks and schedule

Validation depends on Santa Marina confirming the four pending legal bases. Schedule risk remains open: if confirmation arrives after August, the final load and pilot must be rescheduled. An alternative date will not be treated as approved until formal communication is received.

The deliverable must clearly distinguish the plan date from a change proposal. Metrics, annexes, and examples will be reviewed in both the editable source and PDF. Required signatures are those of Javier Ortega Campos and Luis Noguera.

10. Conclusions

The approach transforms the catalogue without hiding uncertainty. Separating missing, non-applicable, excluded, and pending values was essential to avoid false errors and complete the model without inventing data. Compound identifiers remove collisions, and regression tests reduce the risk of recurrence.

The candidate version may proceed to pre-production once municipal confirmations are incorporated, full validation is repeated, and the signed report is archived. Registration data remains outside the publishable scope until a sufficient formal licence exists.

Every publishable record must include an identified source, extraction date, licence, owner, validation result, and relation to its previous version where applicable. Transformed values must retain the source field. Isolated manual corrections are not accepted.

Annex B. Rerun procedure

The rerun starts from a clean copy, installs the exact ontology and shape versions, loads the manifest, transforms the records, executes the rules, and generates two outputs: a readable report and a structured file. Checksums are compared before approval.

questions.question: How must the LUMEN public package be generated, and which actions are required when an object that was already available is withdrawn?

gt_evidences.text: The public package is generated from a positive list of approved objects. It does not begin with every file and exclude later. An automated check compares the list, manifest, and resulting files.

Withdrawals have an identifier, reason, date, and owner. The object stops being displayed, while its record may retain metadata where authorized. Caches and thumbnails are deleted, and deletion is verified.

ranked_retrieved_results.content: LUMEN COLLECTION WORK PLAN AND GOVERNANCE V1.0 1. Purpose LUMEN develops a bilingual knowledge graph for collections held by the Regional Archive of the Centre. The project connects objects, people, places, dates, document types, events, and rights while retaining original description and uncertainty. It does not seek to replace archival systems or turn an interpretation into a definitive fact. The plan covers source selection, terminology, modeling, ingestion, disambiguation, rights, the demonstrator, evaluation, and publication. Every activity must produce verifiable evidence. A coordination conversation does not itself alter a licence, model, or object selection; the decision must be recorded and approved by the competent party. 2. Principles The Regional Archive validates meaning, context, and conditions of use. NEXUS designs transformations, software, tests, and documentation. Original data is retained alongside normalized values. A date such as “spring 1947” keeps its literal and receives an interpreted interval. A term without an exact equivalent retains its source term.

ranked_retrieved_results.content: LUMEN SECOND INGESTION AND DATA QUALITY REPORT V1.0 1. Summary The second LUMEN ingestion added 1,180 municipal correspondence letters and updated records from photography, posters, and person authorities. The batch was processed after applying terminology guide v1.1, the approximate-date schema, and corrections arising from the first linking evaluation. The run received 1,180 letter records and 1,164 digital files. Sixteen letters had no associated image but retained authorized metadata. The system processed every record and isolated errors without silently reducing counts. 2. Results Initial validation identified forty-seven non-normalized dates, twenty-nine ambiguous senders, eighteen place names without a sufficient candidate, twelve files with checksums differing from the manifest, and nine pending rights values. The twelve files were replaced with verified copies before processing continued. After correction, zero critical errors remained. Twenty-four person mentions remain unlinked, eleven places remain open, and nine objects remain outside the demonstrator because rights are pending. 3.

- **Projects & Frameworks**: SILEX (bilingual municipal systems dataset) includes 7 work packages, deliverables, SHACL validation, and risks (legal delays, data mapping gaps). ORION creates NEXUS entity data packages; ARIADNA benchmarks retrieval with 2,302 bilingual questions (recall@10: hybrid 0.80 vs. BM25 0.69). VERDANT ENERGY standardizes energy data (installations, quality codes).  
- **Ontologies & Data Models**: SILEX v1.1 uses language-independent identifiers and bilingual labels (`PublicService`). LUMEN defines archival terms (ES/EN); SolCentro specifies energy data fields.  
- **Validation & Testing**: SILEX Mapping Report resolved 63 violations (96.4% completeness) to 4 legal issues. ARIADNA evaluates systems via recall@10, hybrid models improve multi-hop queries but increase latency. Testing includes authentication, access control, and failure classification (blocking/major/minor).  
- **Governance & Controls**: Projects require version-controlled deliverables, legal confirmations, and data minimization policies. Controls (environment separation, logging) have owners, frequency, and evidence requirements; failures exclude datasets from products.  
- **Storage/Access Control**: Immutable storage, encryption, and retention policies; restricted spaces avoid personal sync. VERDANT API enforces policy checks, authentication, and 15-minute data restrictions.  
- **Risks & Limitations**: Risks include legal delays (SILEX), translation errors (LUMEN), and unresolved entity disambiguation (94% precision). Limitations: small sample sizes, multilingual model dependence (ARIADNA), incomplete documentation, and cross-system consistency issues (e.g., conflicting section numbering).  
- **Procurement/Maintenance**: Atlas-2 storage expansion prioritized Offer B (EUR 38,450, 120 TB, 5-year warranty). Maintenance includes firmware updates and post-upgrade verification (84 TB → 196 TB).  
- **Recruitment/Onboarding**: 12-month data engineer plan requires Python/SQL/version control; onboarding includes 1-week setup across ARIADNA/LUMEN/VERDANT systems.

Source content: Every load will have a manifest, checksum, date, licence, source system, and owner. Transformations will preserve the original value where normalization changes its form. Corrected errors will remain linked to the earlier version for auditing.

6. Validation and acceptance

Validation will combine schema checks, SHACL shapes, regression tests, and manual review. Minimum criteria are zero duplicate identifiers, zero critical errors, complete language labels, at least 95% completeness for mandatory fields, and ES/EN result equivalence of at least 98%. Accepted warnings must correspond to known exceptions.

The API must respond in less than two seconds at the 95th percentile for the agreed queries. Users will complete six tasks. A defect is considered blocking if it prevents discovery of a procedure, displays an incorrect deadline, loses context when language changes, or exposes unauthorized data.

7. Communication and change control

Formal communications will use email and remain linked to the corresponding document or decision. Chats support coordination but do not replace approval. Changes to scope, date, licence, or acceptance criteria require a request containing reason, impact, alternatives, and owners.

The current plan will remain available when a revision is published. A new version will state which sections changed and from what date they apply. History will not be rewritten to make a provisional proposal appear to have been approved from the beginning.

R1. Incomplete mappings

Fields without a responsible unit or legal basis may prevent transformation. Mitigation consists of requesting a new export, explicitly marking pending values, and not inferring information absent from an authorized source.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

R2. Duplicate identifiers

Reuse of local codes may cause collisions. Identifiers will combine the source system, procedure type, and local number, and a regression test will prevent recurrence.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

8. Incidents and changes

Any unexpected access, loss, erroneous publication, or use for a different purpose will be reported to the municipal owner and UPSC privacy functions. Affected processing will stop, secure traces will be retained, and scope, cause, and correction will be documented.

A change in scope, participant, dataset, technology, or purpose may require a new assessment. Urgent changes may be applied to reduce risk, but expansion of use will never be presumed from silence.

9. Recommendations

First, continue the pilot using procedure metadata and synthetic data while the registration-data licence is resolved. Second, add legal classification to every load manifest. Third, technically separate internal and public environments. Fourth, make licence review a release criterion. Fifth, preserve the history of legal versions.

Sixth, identify in the transfer record which products are delivered and which remain restricted. Seventh, delete temporary copies at the end. Eighth, train the team in purpose, minimization, and reporting. Ninth, review access periodically. Tenth, do not present provisional authorization as final.

10. Conclusion

SILEX can proceed without using personal content from the municipal register. The core of the pilot is based on administrative metadata and interoperability rules. Legal uncertainty must appear as an explicit restriction rather than be hidden by a technical decision.

The corpus contains documents, emails, chats, notes, and events in Spanish and English. Every bilingual pair represents the same semantic content while using natural wording in each language. Conceptual identifiers, relations, and inclusion decisions must be equivalent across both versions.

2. Principles

The design prioritizes traceability, temporal separation, reproducibility, difficulty diversity, and leakage prevention. A question cannot occur in a different partition from its translation, paraphrase, or variant sharing the same answer and evidence. The benchmark distinguishes direct, temporal, multi-hop, version-comparison, and unanswerable questions. It also distinguishes easy, medium, and advanced difficulty. Thirty-four initial failures came from incorrectly normalized dates, twelve from merged places, and nine from collective entities classified as people. Evaluation separates linking defects from defects in normalized data.

Analysis 30

Median review requires forty-two seconds with a clear signal and ninety-six seconds for initials or changing roles. Showing too many candidates increases time without improving decisions. Options are accept, reject, create a provisional entity, or request evidence.

Analysis 31

Approved links support navigation. Unresolved mentions remain visible as text and may be grouped by literal without asserting identity. Pending links are not used in identity questions or open products.

Analysis 32

The recommendation is to retain the 0.88 threshold, require a contextual signal, block temporal incompatibility, classify collective entities before linking, and reevaluate when a collection with a different distribution is added.

Occupation is useful where recorded; period removes impossible candidates; place helps in local collections; and an organization may support a decision. ranked_retrieved_results.content: ARIADNA USER EVALUATION AND CONSENT PROTOCOL V1.0 1. Purpose This protocol defines user evaluation of the ARIADNA system with staff from the Research Office at Sierra Centro Public University. It covers objectives, participants, recruitment, consent, tasks, metrics, collected data, security, retention, analysis, incidents, and closure. The study evaluates whether people can locate answers, interpret citations, distinguish current versions, understand abstention, and use language switching. It does not assess individual job performance or make decisions about participants. 2. Background A preliminary test with eight people produced thirty-seven comments. Three high-priority issues were identified: citation links did not always open the exact passage, answers did not clearly show when a policy was superseded, and the absence message did not distinguish missing evidence from retrieval failure. Priority corrections must be verified before the main evaluation. History and export functions are treated as future improvements rather than entry conditions. 3. Participants Recruitment targets twelve to sixteen Research Office staff with varied experience in projects, travel, policies, calls, and administration. Participation is voluntary.

ranked_retrieved_results.content: ARIADNA EVALUATION REPORT V1.0 Document status This report records the first complete ARIADNA evaluation. After it was prepared, possible leakage across tuning and test splits was identified. Version 1.0 therefore remains archived and must not be used as the official performance reference. The original run reported recall@10 of 0.94 for the hybrid baseline. No model or index change justified such a large improvement over earlier results. Review found translations, paraphrases, and questions sharing an answer in different partitions. Original methodology The split was initially created by question identifier. This kept technical records separate but did not correctly group semantically equivalent intents. Spanish and English versions shared a parallel relation, although some additional reformulations were not connected. Consequence Question proximity allowed decisions made during tuning to directly benefit test cases. The value of 0.94 does not represent independent generalization. Run files are retained with an affected-result label to support auditing and reproduction of the incident. Incident record 1 Finding 1 affects separated ES/EN translations. Review uses automatic similarity and manual checking. Confirmed cases are grouped under one intent. The affected splits, experiments using the data, and potential effect on conclusions are recorded. The report does not delete the earlier result: it retains it with archived status and a visible explanation.

ranked_retrieved_results.content: ARIADNA QUESTION ANNOTATION GUIDE V1.1 1. Purpose This guide defines how bilingual questions in the ARIADNA benchmark are created, classified, reviewed, and adjudicated. Version 1.1 incorporates revised criteria for temporal questions, multi-hop questions, version comparisons, and unanswerable cases following the reopening of the corpus. Every semantic question has one Spanish and one English version. Both share the intent, category, difficulty, reference answer, required facts, sources, citations, relevant date, and adjudication decision. Wording must be natural in each language and must not be a mechanical translation revealing answer terms. 2. Principles Questions must be answerable using the corpus alone. External knowledge, speculative inference, and subjective preference are not permitted. Difficulty must arise from locating, relating, and understanding evidence rather than deliberately confusing wording. A question remains grouped with its translations, paraphrases, and variants sharing an answer or essential evidence. This grouping prevents leakage across training, development, and test.

ranked_retrieved_results.content: ARIADNA COMPLEX-CASE ADJUDICATION REGISTER V1.0 Purpose This register documents decisions on questions whose category, answer, date, difficulty, or evidence produced disagreement. Every case retains the initial labels, arguments, sources, final decision, and artifacts requiring updates. Procedure Two people review the case before the session. Adjudication consults the complete source rather than snippets alone. The person proposing the question may explain the intent but does not decide alone. The decision applies to the ES/EN pair. Session decisions Twelve cases were resolved. Four questions became temporal because the answer depended on a version valid on a specific date. Three became multi-hop because they required a relation among an event, task, and owner. Two became unanswerable because no explicit final date existed. Three were split or simplified because they contained two separate questions. Examples For a visit extension, a note explains the rationale, while a later email confirms the date. The answer must distinguish proposal from approval. For a pilot date, a provisional calendar cannot be treated as final without formal confirmation.

ranked_retrieved_results.content: ARIADNA BENCHMARK DESIGN AND CORPUS CONSTRUCTION PROTOCOL V1.0 1. Purpose ARIADNA is a bilingual benchmark for evaluating retrieval-augmented generation systems over administrative and scientific documentation from the NEXUS group. The benchmark studies whether a system retrieves relevant evidence, selects the correct temporal version, integrates distributed information, and produces an answer supported by verifiable citations. The corpus contains documents, emails, chats, notes, and events in Spanish and English. Every bilingual pair represents the same semantic content while using natural wording in each language. Conceptual identifiers, relations, and inclusion decisions must be equivalent across both versions. 2. Principles The design prioritizes traceability, temporal separation, reproducibility, difficulty diversity, and leakage prevention. A question cannot occur in a different partition from its translation, paraphrase, or variant sharing the same answer and evidence. Superseded documents are retained for historical questions, while questions about the current state must retrieve the current version. The benchmark distinguishes direct, temporal, multi-hop, version-comparison, and unanswerable questions. It also distinguishes easy, medium, and advanced difficulty. An unanswerable question must genuinely lack sufficient evidence; a retrieval failure does not turn an answerable question into an unanswerable one.

Conceptual identifiers, relations, and inclusion decisions must be equivalent across both versions. 2. Principles The design prioritizes traceability, temporal separation, reproducibility, difficulty diversity, and leakage prevention. A question cannot occur in a different partition from its translation, paraphrase, or variant sharing the same answer and evidence. Superseded documents are retained for historical questions, while questions about the current state must retrieve the current version. The benchmark distinguishes direct, temporal, multi-hop, version-comparison, and unanswerable questions. It also distinguishes easy, medium, and advanced difficulty. An unanswerable question must genuinely lack sufficient evidence; a retrieval failure does not turn an answerable question into an unanswerable one.

ranked_retrieved_results.content: The ARIADNA evaluation rubric assesses answers using seven dimensions: faithfulness (claims supported by evidence), completeness (presence of required elements), relevance (focus on the question), temporal accuracy (date-appropriate facts), citation coverage (locatable evidence for all claims), abstention quality (avoiding invented answers for unanswerable questions), and bilingual consistency (equivalent facts in ES/EN). Each dimension uses a 0–1 scale with qualitative labels, requiring evaluators to record numerators, denominators, scores, and explanations. Claims and expected elements are evaluated separately; unsupported or irrelevant claims reduce faithfulness/relevance. Disagreements are resolved using answers, questions, reference records, and complete sources. Examples illustrate scenarios like faithful but incomplete answers, complete but unfaithful answers, and appropriate abstention. Calibration involves adjudicated examples, with evaluators required to reach minimum agreement before scoring.

ranked_retrieved_results.content: The ARIADNA COMPLEX-CASE ADJUDICATION REGISTER documents decisions on disputed questions, retaining initial labels, arguments, sources, and final decisions. Cases are reviewed by two people using complete sources, not snippets. Of 12 resolved cases, four became temporal (date-dependent), three multi-hop (event-task-owner relations), two unanswerable (no explicit final date), and three split/simplified (multiple independent questions). Examples emphasize distinguishing proposal from approval and requiring formal confirmation for provisional dates. Adjudication rules (1–11) address contradictions (validity, purpose, status), splitting questions into separate parts, and triggering translation reviews for category/answer/citation changes. Reopened cases retain history, and decisions include identifiers, participants, explanations, and update owners. Rules 1, 4, 7, 10 repeat identical content on contradictory sources.

Source content: Every load will have a manifest, checksum, date, licence, source system, and owner. Transformations will preserve the original value where normalization changes its form. Corrected errors will remain linked to the earlier version for auditing.

6. Validation and acceptance

Validation will combine schema checks, SHACL shapes, regression tests, and manual review. Minimum criteria are zero duplicate identifiers, zero critical errors, complete language labels, at least 95% completeness for mandatory fields, and ES/EN result equivalence of at least 98%. Accepted warnings must correspond to known exceptions.

The API must respond in less than two seconds at the 95th percentile for the agreed queries. Users will complete six tasks. A defect is considered blocking if it prevents discovery of a procedure, displays an incorrect deadline, loses context when language changes, or exposes unauthorized data.

7. Communication and change control

Formal communications will use email and remain linked to the corresponding document or decision. Chats support coordination but do not replace approval. Changes to scope, date, licence, or acceptance criteria require a request containing reason, impact, alternatives, and owners.

The current plan will remain available when a revision is published. A new version will state which sections changed and from what date they apply. History will not be rewritten to make a provisional proposal appear to have been approved from the beginning.

R1. Incomplete mappings

Fields without a responsible unit or legal basis may prevent transformation. Mitigation consists of requesting a new export, explicitly marking pending values, and not inferring information absent from an authorized source.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

R2. Duplicate identifiers

Reuse of local codes may cause collisions. Identifiers will combine the source system, procedure type, and local number, and a regression test will prevent recurrence.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

R3. Registration-data licence

Lack of formal confirmation limits scope. Registration data will remain outside the public pilot and will be used in internal tests only where written authorization exists.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

R4. Bilingual inconsistency

Divergent labels or messages may produce different results. Every class, property, status, and API message will be reviewed in parallel and use a shared language-independent identifier.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

R5. Environment delay

Unavailability of municipal infrastructure may shorten testing. An equivalent UPSC environment will be retained, but final acceptance requires repeating checks on the municipal network.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

R6. SHACL false positives

Overly general rules may flag informational procedures as errors. Shapes will be conditional on procedure type, and accepted warnings will include justification.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

R7. Pilot-date change

Source content: ORION FINAL REPORT AND REUSABLE DATA PACKAGE V1.0

1. Summary

ORION consolidated information about projects, publications, datasets, software, and research profiles within the NEXUS group. The final result is a reusable package with stable identifiers, verified relations, provenance, and sufficient documentation for controlled incorporation into ARIADNA and other internal systems.

The package does not reproduce every field from the original system. Internal metrics, audit records, personal addresses, review notes, and attributes without a clear purpose in the reusable product are excluded. Included fields retain their source system and extraction date.

2. Scope

The delivery contains tables for people, affiliations, projects, publications, datasets, software, organizations, and relations. It also includes identity tables, vocabularies, manifests, checksums, transformation rules, and an exclusion inventory.

Eight profiles remain outside the package because their identity could not be resolved with sufficient evidence. Fifteen historical records are retained as controlled distractors and explicitly marked as superseded versions or earlier states.

3. Principles

Reuse is based on traceability, minimization, version control, and separation between source and derived data. An inferred relation does not replace evidence. Profile merges require a recorded decision and retain earlier identifiers through equivalence relations.

Name similarity provides coverage but disambiguates frequent names poorly. Occupation is the strongest individual signal in photography, posters, and minutes. Source content: Every load will have a manifest, checksum, date, licence, source system, and owner. Transformations will preserve the original value where normalization changes its form. Corrected errors will remain linked to the earlier version for auditing.

6. Validation and acceptance

Validation will combine schema checks, SHACL shapes, regression tests, and manual review. Minimum criteria are zero duplicate identifiers, zero critical errors, complete language labels, at least 95% completeness for mandatory fields, and ES/EN result equivalence of at least 98%. Accepted warnings must correspond to known exceptions.

The API must respond in less than two seconds at the 95th percentile for the agreed queries. Users will complete six tasks. A defect is considered blocking if it prevents discovery of a procedure, displays an incorrect deadline, loses context when language changes, or exposes unauthorized data.

7. Communication and change control

Formal communications will use email and remain linked to the corresponding document or decision. Chats support coordination but do not replace approval. Changes to scope, date, licence, or acceptance criteria require a request containing reason, impact, alternatives, and owners.

The current plan will remain available when a revision is published. A new version will state which sections changed and from what date they apply. History will not be rewritten to make a provisional proposal appear to have been approved from the beginning.

R1. Incomplete mappings

Fields without a responsible unit or legal basis may prevent transformation. Mitigation consists of requesting a new export, explicitly marking pending values, and not inferring information absent from an authorized source.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

R2. Duplicate identifiers

Reuse of local codes may cause collisions. Identifiers will combine the source system, procedure type, and local number, and a regression test will prevent recurrence.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

R3. Registration-data licence

Lack of formal confirmation limits scope. Registration data will remain outside the public pilot and will be used in internal tests only where written authorization exists.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

R4. Bilingual inconsistency

Divergent labels or messages may produce different results. Every class, property, status, and API message will be reviewed in parallel and use a shared language-independent identifier.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

R5. Environment delay

Unavailability of municipal infrastructure may shorten testing. An equivalent UPSC environment will be retained, but final acceptance requires repeating checks on the municipal network.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

R6. SHACL false positives

Overly general rules may flag informational procedures as errors. Shapes will be conditional on procedure type, and accepted warnings will include justification.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

questions.question: When ARIADNA's leakage-affected result was replaced by the corrected evaluation, by how much did hybrid recall@10 fall, and what quantitative advantage and latency cost did it retain over BM25?

gt_evidences.text: The original run reported recall@10 of 0.94 for the hybrid baseline. No model or index change justified such a large improvement over earlier results. Review found translations, paraphrases, and questions sharing an answer in different partitions.

BM25 achieves recall@10 of 0.69, MRR of 0.52, and median latency of 74 ms. Hybrid retrieval achieves recall@10 of 0.80, MRR of 0.63, and median latency of 182 ms. Improvement is concentrated in semantic, multi-hop, and temporal questions. BM25 retains an advantage for exact identifiers and highly specific strings.

Earlier results obtained from a split affected by leakage are retained only for auditing and are not used to compare systems. The main evaluation uses recall@10, MRR, latency, and analysis by category. Experiments use 256-token chunks, three seeds where applicable, and the corpus freeze date recorded in the manifest. 2. Systems BM25 serves as the lexical baseline and uses title, tags, and text. Dense retrieval uses a multilingual model. The hybrid system combines lexical and dense scores and applies lightweight reranking. Configurations share the same document collection and version filters. 3. Overall results BM25 achieves recall@10 of 0.69, MRR of 0.52, and median latency of 74 ms. Hybrid retrieval achieves recall@10 of 0.80, MRR of 0.63, and median latency of 182 ms. Improvement is concentrated in semantic, multi-hop, and temporal questions.

The earlier report remains archived because it documents the leakage incident and supports reconstruction of decisions. Its metrics must not be used to compare systems. The official benchmark count is 2,302 semantic questions and 4,604 ES/EN records. The corpus freeze date is 31 May 2026. The pilot is planned for 15 September 2026. 2. Split correction Questions were grouped by semantic intent before assignment to a split. Every group contains translations, paraphrases, variants sharing the same answer, and cases sharing essential evidence. All group members remain together. Reconstruction produced 1,840 training semantic questions, 230 development questions, and 232 test questions. Spanish and English versions remain in the same split. Validation identifies zero orphaned pairs and zero divided groups. 3. Baselines BM25 achieves recall@10 of 0.69 and MRR of 0.52. The hybrid system achieves recall@10 of 0.80 and MRR of 0.63. The earlier value of 0.94 is identified as affected by leakage and is not an official result. Hybrid retrieval improves semantic, multi-hop, and temporal questions in particular. BM25 remains competitive for exact identifiers and low-ambiguity strings.

ranked_retrieved_results.content: ARIADNA EVALUATION REPORT V1.0 Document status This report records the first complete ARIADNA evaluation. After it was prepared, possible leakage across tuning and test splits was identified. Version 1.0 therefore remains archived and must not be used as the official performance reference. The original run reported recall@10 of 0.94 for the hybrid baseline. No model or index change justified such a large improvement over earlier results. Review found translations, paraphrases, and questions sharing an answer in different partitions. Original methodology The split was initially created by question identifier. This kept technical records separate but did not correctly group semantically equivalent intents. Spanish and English versions shared a parallel relation, although some additional reformulations were not connected. Consequence Question proximity allowed decisions made during tuning to directly benefit test cases. The value of 0.94 does not represent independent generalization. Run files are retained with an affected-result label to support auditing and reproduction of the incident. Incident record 1 Finding 1 affects separated ES/EN translations. Review uses automatic similarity and manual checking. Confirmed cases are grouped under one intent. The affected splits, experiments using the data, and potential effect on conclusions are recorded. The report does not delete the earlier result: it retains it with archived status and a visible explanation.

- **Projects & Frameworks**: SILEX (bilingual municipal systems dataset) includes 7 work packages, deliverables, SHACL validation, and risks (legal delays, data mapping gaps). ORION creates NEXUS entity data packages; ARIADNA benchmarks retrieval with 2,302 bilingual questions (recall@10: hybrid 0.80 vs. BM25 0.69). VERDANT ENERGY standardizes energy data (installations, quality codes).  
- **Ontologies & Data Models**: SILEX v1.1 uses language-independent identifiers and bilingual labels (`PublicService`). LUMEN defines archival terms (ES/EN); SolCentro specifies energy data fields.  
- **Validation & Testing**: SILEX Mapping Report resolved 63 violations (96.4% completeness) to 4 legal issues. ARIADNA evaluates systems via recall@10, hybrid models improve multi-hop queries but increase latency. Testing includes authentication, access control, and failure classification (blocking/major/minor).  
- **Governance & Controls**: Projects require version-controlled deliverables, legal confirmations, and data minimization policies. Controls (environment separation, logging) have owners, frequency, and evidence requirements; failures exclude datasets from products.  
- **Storage/Access Control**: Immutable storage, encryption, and retention policies; restricted spaces avoid personal sync. VERDANT API enforces policy checks, authentication, and 15-minute data restrictions.  
- **Risks & Limitations**: Risks include legal delays (SILEX), translation errors (LUMEN), and unresolved entity disambiguation (94% precision). Limitations: small sample sizes, multilingual model dependence (ARIADNA), incomplete documentation, and cross-system consistency issues (e.g., conflicting section numbering).  
- **Procurement/Maintenance**: Atlas-2 storage expansion prioritized Offer B (EUR 38,450, 120 TB, 5-year warranty). Maintenance includes firmware updates and post-upgrade verification (84 TB → 196 TB).  
- **Recruitment/Onboarding**: 12-month data engineer plan requires Python/SQL/version control; onboarding includes 1-week setup across ARIADNA/LUMEN/VERDANT systems.

Source content: ARIADNA RETRIEVAL BASELINE COMPARISON REPORT V1.0

1. Objective

This report compares BM25, dense retrieval, and hybrid retrieval on the corrected ARIADNA split. Earlier results obtained from a split affected by leakage are retained only for auditing and are not used to compare systems.

The main evaluation uses recall@10, MRR, latency, and analysis by category. Experiments use 256-token chunks, three seeds where applicable, and the corpus freeze date recorded in the manifest.

2. Systems

BM25 serves as the lexical baseline and uses title, tags, and text. Dense retrieval uses a multilingual model. The hybrid system combines lexical and dense scores and applies lightweight reranking. Configurations share the same document collection and version filters.

3. Overall results

BM25 achieves recall@10 of 0.69, MRR of 0.52, and median latency of 74 ms. Hybrid retrieval achieves recall@10 of 0.80, MRR of 0.63, and median latency of 182 ms. Improvement is concentrated in semantic, multi-hop, and temporal questions. BM25 retains an advantage for exact identifiers and highly specific strings.

Detailed result 1

Analysis 1: direct questions. Results show that both systems retrieve sources containing explicit terms well. Recall, rank of the first relevant result, number of required sources, and latency are compared. Errors are manually reviewed to distinguish query, index, chunking, version, or relevance defects. Comparison uses confidence intervals and retains individual runs rather than the mean alone. A small difference is not presented as a definitive conclusion.

Detailed result 2

Analysis 2: temporal questions. Results show that hybrid retrieval finds related documents better but requires validity filters. Recall, rank of the first relevant result, number of required sources, and latency are compared. Errors are manually reviewed to distinguish query, index, chunking, version, or relevance defects. Comparison uses confidence intervals and retains individual runs rather than the mean alone. A small difference is not presented as a definitive conclusion.

Detailed result 3

Analysis 3: multi-hop questions. Results show that retrieval of complementary sources improves with dense signals. Recall, rank of the first relevant result, number of required sources, and latency are compared. Errors are manually reviewed to distinguish query, index, chunking, version, or relevance defects. Comparison uses confidence intervals and retains individual runs rather than the mean alone. A small difference is not presented as a definitive conclusion.

Detailed result 4

Analysis 4: version comparison. Results show that BM25 locates version numbers while hybrid retrieval broadens context. Recall, rank of the first relevant result, number of required sources, and latency are compared. Errors are manually reviewed to distinguish query, index, chunking, version, or relevance defects. Comparison uses confidence intervals and retains individual runs rather than the mean alone. A small difference is not presented as a definitive conclusion.

Detailed result 5

Analysis 5: unanswerable questions. Results show that no retriever should be treated as a perfect detector of absence. Recall, rank of the first relevant result, number of required sources, and latency are compared. Errors are manually reviewed to distinguish query, index, chunking, version, or relevance defects. Comparison uses confidence intervals and retains individual runs rather than the mean alone. A small difference is not presented as a definitive conclusion.

Detailed result 6

Experiment 1 compares C256 versus C512. The corpus, split, questions, and evaluation remain fixed. Any additional change is recorded as a separate factor. Results contain the exact configuration, seed, chunk count, and index checksum. Final selection considers effectiveness, operating cost, explainability, and cross-language stability. A configuration is not selected from one aggregate metric alone.

Claim: Changes to scope, date, licence, or acceptance criteria require a request containing reason, impact, alternatives, and owners.
Source content: Every load will have a manifest, checksum, date, licence, source system, and owner. Transformations will preserve the original value where normalization changes its form. Corrected errors will remain linked to the earlier version for auditing.

6. Validation and acceptance

Validation will combine schema checks, SHACL shapes, regression tests, and manual review. Minimum criteria are zero duplicate identifiers, zero critical errors, complete language labels, at least 95% completeness for mandatory fields, and ES/EN result equivalence of at least 98%. Accepted warnings must correspond to known exceptions.

The API must respond in less than two seconds at the 95th percentile for the agreed queries. Users will complete six tasks. A defect is considered blocking if it prevents discovery of a procedure, displays an incorrect deadline, loses context when language changes, or exposes unauthorized data.

7. Communication and change control

Formal communications will use email and remain linked to the corresponding document or decision. Chats support coordination but do not replace approval. Changes to scope, date, licence, or acceptance criteria require a request containing reason, impact, alternatives, and owners.

The current plan will remain available when a revision is published. A new version will state which sections changed and from what date they apply. History will not be rewritten to make a provisional proposal appear to have been approved from the beginning.

R1. Incomplete mappings

Fields without a responsible unit or legal basis may prevent transformation. Mitigation consists of requesting a new export, explicitly marking pending values, and not inferring information absent from an authorized source.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

R2. Duplicate identifiers

Reuse of local codes may cause collisions. Identifiers will combine the source system, procedure type, and local number, and a regression test will prevent recurrence.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

R3. Registration-data licence

Lack of formal confirmation limits scope. Registration data will remain outside the public pilot and will be used in internal tests only where written authorization exists.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

R4. Bilingual inconsistency

Divergent labels or messages may produce different results. Every class, property, status, and API message will be reviewed in parallel and use a shared language-independent identifier.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

R5. Environment delay

Unavailability of municipal infrastructure may shorten testing. An equivalent UPSC environment will be retained, but final acceptance requires repeating checks on the municipal network.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

R6. SHACL false positives

Overly general rules may flag informational procedures as errors. Shapes will be conditional on procedure type, and accepted warnings will include justification.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

R7. Pilot-date change

ranked_retrieved_results.content: DELIVERABLE D3 — SILEX MAPPING AND VALIDATION REPORT This report documents the method used to transform the municipal catalogue into the SILEX ontology, the batch 3 validation results, agreed corrections, and criteria for accepting the candidate version. It retains both initial and post-correction results so the effect of every change can be verified. Batch 3 contains 412 records. The first run produced sixty-three violations across forty-one records: twenty-eight missing competent units, seventeen non-normalized dates, eleven duplicate identifiers, and seven statuses outside the vocabulary. Nine channel warnings were also identified as false positives. 1. Sources and scope Sources are the revised Santa Marina catalogue, ontology specification v1.1, auxiliary unit and legal-basis tables, and status and channel vocabularies. Validation does not include individual cases or registration-data content. Personal examples used during development are synthetic. Mapping covers identifiers, titles, descriptions, units, legal bases, channels, deadlines, statuses, provenance, and version relations. Local presentation fields are excluded where they add no interoperable meaning. Every exclusion includes its reason and source system.

Purpose and scope This plan defines the organization of the SILEX pilot phase, whose purpose is to determine whether a heterogeneous municipal catalogue can be transformed into an interoperable, bilingual, and verifiable semantic representation. The pilot is jointly conducted by the NEXUS group at Sierra Centro Public University and the Santa Marina City Council. Its scope covers procedure selection, field mapping, ontology publication, data validation, API deployment, and evaluation with municipal staff. The plan does not itself authorize reuse of every available dataset. Each source retains its own licence and access conditions. In particular, the municipal register of residents is treated as restricted until the municipal legal office confirms permitted uses in writing. Technical availability of an export will not be interpreted as authorization to publish or redistribute it. Version 1.0 uses 15 September 2026 as the reference date for the start of the pilot. If mappings, licences, or the environment make that date infeasible, project management will prepare a change proposal. An alternative date remains provisional until formally approved by the steering committee and confirmed in writing by the municipality.

ranked_retrieved_results.content: SILEX PILOT FINAL EVALUATION REPORT V1.0 1. Executive summary The final SILEX pilot evaluation was conducted with ten participants from the Santa Marina City Council between 7 and 14 October 2026. Participants represented citizen services, urban planning, trade, environment, the general secretariat, and electronic administration. Every participant completed six procedure-search and review tasks followed by a questionnaire and short interview. Evaluation measured success, time, requests for help, clarity, ease of search, ES/EN consistency, and confidence in deadlines and legal bases. The overall success rate was 88%. Median task time was 2 minutes 18 seconds. Language switching preserved the query and entity in 100% of journeys. The API achieved p95 latency of 1.42 seconds during sessions. No exposure of restricted data was identified. 2. Scope Tasks covered locating a procedure, identifying the competent unit, checking a channel, interpreting a deadline, comparing a legal version, and switching language. Authorized procedures and data without personal cases were used. The evaluation does not measure large-scale citizen use and does not replace a complete accessibility audit. Results apply to the environment, corpus, and versions recorded in the manifest.

ranked_retrieved_results.content: SILEX ONTOLOGY SPECIFICATION V1.1 The SILEX ontology represents municipal services and procedures, their units, channels, legal bases, deadlines, statuses, and version relations. Version 1.1 is the basis for the initial mappings and will be superseded by version 1.2 after bilingual labels and constraints identified during validation are corrected. Class and property identifiers are language independent. Spanish and English labels express the same concept and are reviewed together. An editorial change does not change the identifier; an incompatible semantic change requires a documented new version. Version pattern Every versioned resource may declare a previous version, next version, start of validity, and end of validity. Version relations must be reciprocal, must not form cycles, and remain within the same document language. Cross-language equivalence is expressed through a separate parallel relation. silex:PublicService — Public service Class for a provision organized by a public administration. It must not be translated as public procedure because one service may offer several procedures and channels. Approved Spanish label: “Servicio público”. The class must include a definition, example, and provenance.

ranked_retrieved_results.content: SILEX API SPECIFICATION V1.0 Purpose The SILEX API provides controlled access to the semantic catalogue of municipal procedures. It supports procedure discovery, record retrieval, vocabulary access, identifier validation, and version information. The specification defines endpoints, parameters, authentication, responses, errors, and bilingual requirements. Base and version The base path is `/api/silex/v1`. Incompatible changes require a new major version. Compatible changes may add optional fields but must not change the meaning of existing fields. Every response contains the API version, catalogue version, and generation date. Authentication The municipal environment uses VPN access and named credentials. Secrets are not included in examples or logs. Shared accounts are not permitted. Administrative access is separate from query access. Languages The `lang` parameter accepts `es` or `en`. Identifiers and error codes are language independent. Labels, descriptions, and visible messages are returned in the requested language. Where a translation is missing, the response states the available language and does not mix both languages in one literal.
