ranked_retrieved_results.content: 2. Delivery principles SILEX follows five principles. First, values will not be invented to fill missing data. Second, every change will be traceable to a source, responsible person, and date. Third, the Spanish and English versions will share identifiers and meaning. Fourth, validation will occur before publication or deployment. Fifth, legal and organizational decisions take precedence over technical availability. Data will be classified as present, missing, non-applicable, excluded, or awaiting validation. This distinction is mandatory because it affects SHACL rules, interface presentation, and metric interpretation. An empty field alone is not sufficient to express its status. 3. Governance Javier Ortega Campos acts as scientific lead and contact point with Santa Marina. Luis Noguera coordinates municipal staff and validates local names, units, and processes. Mireia Soler Pons leads ontology work; Alba Prieto Mora maintains the catalogue and test data; Nuria Castaño Rey manages deployment and security; Sergio Vidal Cruz administers storage, ingestion, and backups; Clara Ibáñez Soto coordinates budget, evidence, and closure. The steering committee will meet monthly and whenever a critical blocker arises. Decisions will be classified as approved, provisional, or rejected.

Final acceptance depends on municipal validation and repetition of full validation.

ranked_retrieved_results.content: The ARIADNA evaluation rubric assesses answers using seven dimensions: faithfulness (claims supported by evidence), completeness (presence of required elements), relevance (focus on the question), temporal accuracy (date-appropriate facts), citation coverage (locatable evidence for all claims), abstention quality (avoiding invented answers for unanswerable questions), and bilingual consistency (equivalent facts in ES/EN). Each dimension uses a 0–1 scale with qualitative labels, requiring evaluators to record numerators, denominators, scores, and explanations. Claims and expected elements are evaluated separately; unsupported or irrelevant claims reduce faithfulness/relevance. Disagreements are resolved using answers, questions, reference records, and complete sources. Examples illustrate scenarios like faithful but incomplete answers, complete but unfaithful answers, and appropriate abstention. Calibration involves adjudicated examples, with evaluators required to reach minimum agreement before scoring.

5. Duplicate-identifier incident

The regression test searches for repetition within the batch, across previous loads, and among different types. It also verifies that references to documents and units are updated with the new identifier. The old source code is retained as an alternative identifier with provenance.

6. SHACL-shape adjustments

The channel shape required at least one value for every record. This was incorrect for purely informational records. The new rule applies cardinality only to procedures that accept an application or provide an operational service. Informational records may declare the field non-applicable.

The date rule is extended to accept a year, interval, or exact date but not free text without an assessment. Bilingual labels are checked by base identifier. The version shape prevents cycles and requires reciprocity between previous and next versions.

7. Regression set

The set contains twenty-four procedures not used during diagnosis: six permits, five certificates, four grants, four prior notifications, and five informational records. It checks the identifier, unit, legal basis, channel, deadline, status, and labels.

It contains two non-applicable cases and three pending fields to prevent corrections from turning explicit states into gaps. The expected result is zero duplicates and zero labels without a language. A recurring failure blocks publication of ontology v1.2.

8. Post-correction results

The second run reduced critical violations to four records with legal bases awaiting municipal validation. These cases will not be published as complete and will retain the pending assessment. Duplicates, date formats, and unmapped statuses were corrected.

The nine channel warnings disappeared after the rule became conditional. Comparison of reports confirms that no correction removed original information. ES/EN label coverage reached 100% in the batch, and completeness of publishable mandatory fields was 96.4%.

9. Risks and schedule

Validation depends on Santa Marina confirming the four pending legal bases. Schedule risk remains open: if confirmation arrives after August, the final load and pilot must be rescheduled. An alternative date will not be treated as approved until formal communication is received.

The approach transforms the catalogue without hiding uncertainty. Compound identifiers remove collisions, and regression tests reduce the risk of recurrence.

The rerun starts from a clean copy, installs the exact ontology and shape versions, loads the manifest, transforms the records, executes the rules, and generates two outputs: a readable report and a structured file. Checksums are compared before approval.

1. Executive summary

The final SILEX pilot evaluation was conducted with ten participants from the Santa Marina City Council between 7 and 14 October 2026. Participants represented citizen services, urban planning, trade, environment, the general secretariat, and electronic administration.

Every participant completed six procedure-search and review tasks followed by a questionnaire and short interview. Evaluation measured success, time, requests for help, clarity, ease of search, ES/EN consistency, and confidence in deadlines and legal bases.

The overall success rate was 88%. Median task time was 2 minutes 18 seconds. Language switching preserved the query and entity in 100% of journeys. The API achieved p95 latency of 1.42 seconds during sessions. No exposure of restricted data was identified.

2. Scope

Tasks covered locating a procedure, identifying the competent unit, checking a channel, interpreting a deadline, comparing a legal version, and switching language. Authorized procedures and data without personal cases were used.

The evaluation does not measure large-scale citizen use and does not replace a complete accessibility audit. Results apply to the environment, corpus, and versions recorded in the manifest.

3. Method

Tasks had verifiable answers and success criteria. Five participants began in Spanish and five in English. Order was alternated to reduce learning effects. Observers recorded actions and assistance but not the content of personal searches.

Comments were classified by severity, frequency, and scope. A critical defect blocked the pilot; a major defect required priority correction; a minor defect could move to the improvement plan.

Evaluation section 1

Task 1 was to locate a minor building permit. The objective was to search by text and verify that the correct record appears among the first results. Complete success, partial success, failure, time, action count, assistance, and comments were recorded. Review compared the answer with the source and distinguished a data, interface, wording, or training defect. Results were analyzed by language and profile. An ambiguous task was reviewed before attributing the problem to the system.

1. Purpose

ARIADNA is a bilingual benchmark for evaluating retrieval-augmented generation systems over administrative and scientific documentation from the NEXUS group. The benchmark studies whether a system retrieves relevant evidence, selects the correct temporal version, integrates distributed information, and produces an answer supported by verifiable citations.

The corpus contains documents, emails, chats, notes, and events in Spanish and English. Every bilingual pair represents the same semantic content while using natural wording in each language. Conceptual identifiers, relations, and inclusion decisions must be equivalent across both versions.

2. Principles

The design prioritizes traceability, temporal separation, reproducibility, difficulty diversity, and leakage prevention. A question cannot occur in a different partition from its translation, paraphrase, or variant sharing the same answer and evidence. Superseded documents are retained for historical questions, while questions about the current state must retrieve the current version.

The benchmark distinguishes direct, temporal, multi-hop, version-comparison, and unanswerable questions. It also distinguishes easy, medium, and advanced difficulty. An unanswerable question must genuinely lack sufficient evidence; a retrieval failure does not turn an answerable question into an unanswerable one.

3. Scope

The first official version contains 2,302 semantic questions and 4,604 language records. Every semantic question has one Spanish and one English version. The corpus uses artifacts from SILEX, LUMEN, VERDANT, ARIADNA, ORION, and LabOps. The source freeze date is recorded in the manifest.

Reference answers contain expected facts, citations, acceptable alternative sources, relevant date, and non-answer conditions. The benchmark does not require one exact wording, but every important claim must be covered by evidence.

Methodology section 1

Category 1, direct questions, is used where one source contains the main answer. Every question records its intent, difficulty, answer, required facts, sources, citations, and reference date. The annotator must justify why the category is appropriate and state discarded alternatives. ES/EN pairs share category, evidence, and decision even where wording is naturally adapted. Review checks that the question does not depend on external knowledge or an interpretation unsupported by the corpus.

The annotator must justify why the category is appropriate and state discarded alternatives. ES/EN pairs share category, evidence, and decision even where wording is naturally adapted. Claim: The overall success rate was 88%.
Entity: SILEX (ORGANIZATION)
Entity: Santa Marina City Council (ORGANIZATION)
Relation: SILEX --EVALUATED_BY--> Santa Marina City Council
Relation evidence: The final SILEX pilot evaluation was conducted with ten participants from the Santa Marina City Council between 7 and 14 October 2026.
Source content: SILEX PILOT FINAL EVALUATION REPORT V1.0

1. Executive summary

The final SILEX pilot evaluation was conducted with ten participants from the Santa Marina City Council between 7 and 14 October 2026. Participants represented citizen services, urban planning, trade, environment, the general secretariat, and electronic administration.

Every participant completed six procedure-search and review tasks followed by a questionnaire and short interview. Evaluation measured success, time, requests for help, clarity, ease of search, ES/EN consistency, and confidence in deadlines and legal bases.

The overall success rate was 88%. Median task time was 2 minutes 18 seconds. Language switching preserved the query and entity in 100% of journeys. The API achieved p95 latency of 1.42 seconds during sessions. No exposure of restricted data was identified.

2. Scope

Tasks covered locating a procedure, identifying the competent unit, checking a channel, interpreting a deadline, comparing a legal version, and switching language. Authorized procedures and data without personal cases were used.

The evaluation does not measure large-scale citizen use and does not replace a complete accessibility audit. Results apply to the environment, corpus, and versions recorded in the manifest.

3. Method

Tasks had verifiable answers and success criteria. Five participants began in Spanish and five in English. Order was alternated to reduce learning effects. Observers recorded actions and assistance but not the content of personal searches.

Comments were classified by severity, frequency, and scope. A critical defect blocked the pilot; a major defect required priority correction; a minor defect could move to the improvement plan.

Evaluation section 1

SILEX PILOT FINAL EVALUATION REPORT V1.0

1. Executive summary

The final SILEX pilot evaluation was conducted with ten participants from the Santa Marina City Council between 7 and 14 October 2026. Participants represented citizen services, urban planning, trade, environment, the general secretariat, and electronic administration.

Every participant completed six procedure-search and review tasks followed by a questionnaire and short interview. Evaluation measured success, time, requests for help, clarity, ease of search, ES/EN consistency, and confidence in deadlines and legal bases.

The overall success rate was 88%. Median task time was 2 minutes 18 seconds. Language switching preserved the query and entity in 100% of journeys. The API achieved p95 latency of 1.42 seconds during sessions. No exposure of restricted data was identified.

2. Scope

Tasks covered locating a procedure, identifying the competent unit, checking a channel, interpreting a deadline, comparing a legal version, and switching language. Authorized procedures and data without personal cases were used.

The evaluation does not measure large-scale citizen use and does not replace a complete accessibility audit. Results apply to the environment, corpus, and versions recorded in the manifest.

3. Method

Tasks had verifiable answers and success criteria. Five participants began in Spanish and five in English. Order was alternated to reduce learning effects. Observers recorded actions and assistance but not the content of personal searches.

Comments were classified by severity, frequency, and scope. A critical defect blocked the pilot; a major defect required priority correction; a minor defect could move to the improvement plan.

6. Validation and acceptance

Validation will combine schema checks, SHACL shapes, regression tests, and manual review. Minimum criteria are zero duplicate identifiers, zero critical errors, complete language labels, at least 95% completeness for mandatory fields, and ES/EN result equivalence of at least 98%. Accepted warnings must correspond to known exceptions.

The API must respond in less than two seconds at the 95th percentile for the agreed queries. Users will complete six tasks. A defect is considered blocking if it prevents discovery of a procedure, displays an incorrect deadline, loses context when language changes, or exposes unauthorized data.

7. Communication and change control

Formal communications will use email and remain linked to the corresponding document or decision. Chats support coordination but do not replace approval. Changes to scope, date, licence, or acceptance criteria require a request containing reason, impact, alternatives, and owners.

The current plan will remain available when a revision is published. A new version will state which sections changed and from what date they apply. History will not be rewritten to make a provisional proposal appear to have been approved from the beginning.

R1. Incomplete mappings

Fields without a responsible unit or legal basis may prevent transformation. Mitigation consists of requesting a new export, explicitly marking pending values, and not inferring information absent from an authorized source.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

R2. Duplicate identifiers

Reuse of local codes may cause collisions. Identifiers will combine the source system, procedure type, and local number, and a regression test will prevent recurrence.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

Unavailability of municipal infrastructure may shorten testing. An equivalent UPSC environment will be retained, but final acceptance requires repeating checks on the municipal network.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

Overly general rules may flag informational procedures as errors. Shapes will be conditional on procedure type, and accepted warnings will include justification.

ranked_retrieved_results.content: HISTORICAL-PERSON LINKING EVALUATION REPORT 1. Objective This report evaluates person linking in descriptions of photography, correspondence, posters, minutes, and inventories. The objective is not to resolve every mention but to obtain links precise enough that navigation and identity questions do not propagate errors. The system generates candidates from the name and uses occupation, dates, places, organizations, collections, and relations. High-confidence cases are accepted; intermediate cases are reviewed; insufficient cases remain unlinked. An open mention is preferable to a false merge. 2. Set The set contains six hundred mentions. Three hundred have a reference entity, 180 concern known but ambiguous people, and 120 cannot be resolved using available sources. It includes frequent names, initials, variants, transcription errors, collective entities, and role changes. Two people reviewed every case. Disagreements were adjudicated with support from the Regional Archive. The split is made by entity rather than mention to avoid references to one person appearing in both development and test.

ranked_retrieved_results.content:
- **Objective & Scope**: Evaluates precision of historical person linking in documents (photography, correspondence, etc.), prioritizing accuracy over completeness. Focuses on resolving mentions with sufficient confidence to prevent error propagation.  
- **Dataset**: 600 mentions (300 resolvable, 180 ambiguous, 120 unresolved). Includes variants, initials, transcription errors, and collective entities. Reviewed by two experts with Regional Archive adjudication.  
- **Method**: Candidate generation normalizes names, uses contextual signals (occupation, dates, places), and applies thresholds (automatic link >0.88, review 0.65–0.88, unlinked <0.65). Temporal incompatibility blocks automatic links.  
- **Results**: Overall precision 0.94, coverage 0.78. Automatic precision 0.98; 29% reviewed, 21% unresolved. Lowering thresholds increases false merges.  
- **Analysis Categories**:  
  - **Namesakes**: Contextual signals (occupation, period, place) required for disambiguation; no single derived relation justifies links.  
  - **Initials**: Same contextual signal requirements as namesakes.  
- **Challenges**: Name similarity poorly disambiguates frequent names; errors from normalized data (dates, merged places, collective entities).  
- **Recommendations**: Retain 0.88 threshold, require contextual signals, block temporal incompatibility, classify collective entities pre-linking, and reevaluate with new data.  
- **Unresolved Cases**: Retain literals, context, and candidates for future review. Pending links excluded from identity queries.

ARIADNA is a bilingual benchmark for evaluating retrieval-augmented generation systems over administrative and scientific documentation from the NEXUS group. The benchmark studies whether a system retrieves relevant evidence, selects the correct temporal version, integrates distributed information, and produces an answer supported by verifiable citations.

The corpus contains documents, emails, chats, notes, and events in Spanish and English. Every bilingual pair represents the same semantic content while using natural wording in each language. Conceptual identifiers, relations, and inclusion decisions must be equivalent across both versions.

2. Principles

The design prioritizes traceability, temporal separation, reproducibility, difficulty diversity, and leakage prevention. A question cannot occur in a different partition from its translation, paraphrase, or variant sharing the same answer and evidence. Superseded documents are retained for historical questions, while questions about the current state must retrieve the current version.

The benchmark distinguishes direct, temporal, multi-hop, version-comparison, and unanswerable questions. It also distinguishes easy, medium, and advanced difficulty. An unanswerable question must genuinely lack sufficient evidence; a retrieval failure does not turn an answerable question into an unanswerable one.

3. Scope

The first official version contains 2,302 semantic questions and 4,604 language records. Every semantic question has one Spanish and one English version. The corpus uses artifacts from SILEX, LUMEN, VERDANT, ARIADNA, ORION, and LabOps. The source freeze date is recorded in the manifest.

Reference answers contain expected facts, citations, acceptable alternative sources, relevant date, and non-answer conditions. The benchmark does not require one exact wording, but every important claim must be covered by evidence.

Source content: Every load will have a manifest, checksum, date, licence, source system, and owner. Transformations will preserve the original value where normalization changes its form. Corrected errors will remain linked to the earlier version for auditing.

6. Validation and acceptance

Validation will combine schema checks, SHACL shapes, regression tests, and manual review. Minimum criteria are zero duplicate identifiers, zero critical errors, complete language labels, at least 95% completeness for mandatory fields, and ES/EN result equivalence of at least 98%. Accepted warnings must correspond to known exceptions.

The API must respond in less than two seconds at the 95th percentile for the agreed queries. Users will complete six tasks. A defect is considered blocking if it prevents discovery of a procedure, displays an incorrect deadline, loses context when language changes, or exposes unauthorized data.

7. Communication and change control

Formal communications will use email and remain linked to the corresponding document or decision. Chats support coordination but do not replace approval. Changes to scope, date, licence, or acceptance criteria require a request containing reason, impact, alternatives, and owners.

The current plan will remain available when a revision is published. A new version will state which sections changed and from what date they apply. History will not be rewritten to make a provisional proposal appear to have been approved from the beginning.

R1. Incomplete mappings

Fields without a responsible unit or legal basis may prevent transformation. Mitigation consists of requesting a new export, explicitly marking pending values, and not inferring information absent from an authorized source.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

R2. Duplicate identifiers

Reuse of local codes may cause collisions. Identifiers will combine the source system, procedure type, and local number, and a regression test will prevent recurrence.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

R3. Registration-data licence

Lack of formal confirmation limits scope. Registration data will remain outside the public pilot and will be used in internal tests only where written authorization exists.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

R4. Bilingual inconsistency

Divergent labels or messages may produce different results. Every class, property, status, and API message will be reviewed in parallel and use a shared language-independent identifier.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

R5. Environment delay

Unavailability of municipal infrastructure may shorten testing. An equivalent UPSC environment will be retained, but final acceptance requires repeating checks on the municipal network.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

R6. SHACL false positives

Overly general rules may flag informational procedures as errors. Shapes will be conditional on procedure type, and accepted warnings will include justification.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

R7. Pilot-date change

1. Executive summary

The VERDANT pilot evaluated federated exchange of energy products among SolCentro, NEXUS, and Instituto Técnico do Norte. The architecture retained original fifteen-minute readings within SolCentro and delivered hourly or daily products subject to policy, purpose, minimum group size, and expiry.

The pilot processed data from sixty-two installations over eighty-nine days. Hourly products were generated where four valid intervals and at least three meters were available. Consumers received metadata, coverage, quality, and provenance together with the aggregate value.

All critical authentication, authorization, revocation, network, logging, and minimum-group tests passed. No exposure of individual readings, names, addresses, contracts, or secrets was identified. Product-request p95 latency was 1.68 seconds in the pre-production environment.

2. Objectives

Objectives were to demonstrate interoperability across connectors, enforce access policies, produce reproducible aggregates, preserve provenance, measure quality, and assess the usefulness of products for energy analysis.

Evaluation does not cover billing, automated installation control, or citizen use. Results apply to the versions, organizations, and period recorded in the manifest.

Source content: Case 2, María López, distinguishes a letter sender and an actress. The decision retains discarded candidates and evidence. Mentions without sufficient occupation, date, place, or organization remain open. The system does not turn an activity interval into a birth or death date. Facts in the record link to specific documents. Where a later source provides a new signal, the case may be reopened without losing review history.

Analysis 25

Case 3, J. Martínez, distinguishes four candidates and many mentions without context. The decision retains discarded candidates and evidence. Mentions without sufficient occupation, date, place, or organization remain open. The system does not turn an activity interval into a birth or death date. Facts in the record link to specific documents. Where a later source provides a new signal, the case may be reopened without losing review history.

Analysis 26

Case 4, Estudio Hermanos Vidal, distinguishes a collective entity initially split as people. The decision retains discarded candidates and evidence. Mentions without sufficient occupation, date, place, or organization remain open. The system does not turn an activity interval into a birth or death date. Facts in the record link to specific documents. Where a later source provides a new signal, the case may be reopened without losing review history.

Analysis 27

Case 5, Ana de la Fuente / Ana Fuente, distinguishes variants accepted only with a matching occupation or address. The decision retains discarded candidates and evidence. Mentions without sufficient occupation, date, place, or organization remain open. The system does not turn an activity interval into a birth or death date. Facts in the record link to specific documents. Where a later source provides a new signal, the case may be reopened without losing review history.

Analysis 28

Name similarity provides coverage but disambiguates frequent names poorly. Occupation is the strongest individual signal in photography, posters, and minutes. Time removes impossible candidates but does not distinguish contemporaries. Explanations containing several signals are more useful than a score alone.

Analysis 29

Thirty-four initial failures came from incorrectly normalized dates, twelve from merged places, and nine from collective entities classified as people. Evaluation separates linking defects from defects in normalized data.

Analysis 30

Median review requires forty-two seconds with a clear signal and ninety-six seconds for initials or changing roles. Showing too many candidates increases time without improving decisions. Options are accept, reject, create a provisional entity, or request evidence.

Analysis 31

Approved links support navigation. Unresolved mentions remain visible as text and may be grouped by literal without asserting identity. Pending links are not used in identity questions or open products.

Analysis 32

The recommendation is to retain the 0.88 threshold, require a contextual signal, block temporal incompatibility, classify collective entities before linking, and reevaluate when a collection with a different distribution is added.

Analysis 33

The design prioritizes traceability, temporal separation, reproducibility, difficulty diversity, and leakage prevention. A question cannot occur in a different partition from its translation, paraphrase, or variant sharing the same answer and evidence. questions.question: By how much did the hybrid system improve over BM25 in recall@10 and MRR in ARIADNA's corrected evaluation?

gt_evidences.text: BM25 achieves recall@10 of 0.69 and MRR of 0.52. The hybrid system achieves recall@10 of 0.80 and MRR of 0.63. The earlier value of 0.94 is identified as affected by leakage and is not an official result.

ranked_retrieved_results.content: ARIADNA RETRIEVAL BASELINE COMPARISON REPORT V1.0 1. Objective This report compares BM25, dense retrieval, and hybrid retrieval on the corrected ARIADNA split. Earlier results obtained from a split affected by leakage are retained only for auditing and are not used to compare systems. The main evaluation uses recall@10, MRR, latency, and analysis by category. Experiments use 256-token chunks, three seeds where applicable, and the corpus freeze date recorded in the manifest. 2. Systems BM25 serves as the lexical baseline and uses title, tags, and text. Dense retrieval uses a multilingual model. The hybrid system combines lexical and dense scores and applies lightweight reranking. Configurations share the same document collection and version filters. 3. Overall results BM25 achieves recall@10 of 0.69, MRR of 0.52, and median latency of 74 ms. Hybrid retrieval achieves recall@10 of 0.80, MRR of 0.63, and median latency of 182 ms. Improvement is concentrated in semantic, multi-hop, and temporal questions.

ranked_retrieved_results.content: ARIADNA EVALUATION REPORT V1.1 1. Status Version 1.1 supersedes report 1.0 and presents results obtained from the corrected split. The earlier report remains archived because it documents the leakage incident and supports reconstruction of decisions. Its metrics must not be used to compare systems. The official benchmark count is 2,302 semantic questions and 4,604 ES/EN records. The corpus freeze date is 31 May 2026. The pilot is planned for 15 September 2026. 2. Split correction Questions were grouped by semantic intent before assignment to a split. Every group contains translations, paraphrases, variants sharing the same answer, and cases sharing essential evidence. All group members remain together. Reconstruction produced 1,840 training semantic questions, 230 development questions, and 232 test questions. Spanish and English versions remain in the same split. Validation identifies zero orphaned pairs and zero divided groups. 3. Baselines BM25 achieves recall@10 of 0.69 and MRR of 0.52. The hybrid system achieves recall@10 of 0.80 and MRR of 0.63. The earlier value of 0.94 is identified as affected by leakage and is not an official result. Hybrid retrieval improves semantic, multi-hop, and temporal questions in particular. BM25 remains competitive for exact identifiers and low-ambiguity strings.

ranked_retrieved_results.content: ARIADNA EVALUATION REPORT V1.0 Document status This report records the first complete ARIADNA evaluation. After it was prepared, possible leakage across tuning and test splits was identified. Version 1.0 therefore remains archived and must not be used as the official performance reference. The original run reported recall@10 of 0.94 for the hybrid baseline. No model or index change justified such a large improvement over earlier results. Review found translations, paraphrases, and questions sharing an answer in different partitions. Original methodology The split was initially created by question identifier. This kept technical records separate but did not correctly group semantically equivalent intents. Spanish and English versions shared a parallel relation, although some additional reformulations were not connected. Consequence Question proximity allowed decisions made during tuning to directly benefit test cases. The value of 0.94 does not represent independent generalization. Run files are retained with an affected-result label to support auditing and reproduction of the incident. Incident record 1 Finding 1 affects separated ES/EN translations. Review uses automatic similarity and manual checking. Confirmed cases are grouped under one intent. The affected splits, experiments using the data, and potential effect on conclusions are recorded. The report does not delete the earlier result: it retains it with archived status and a visible explanation.

- **Projects & Frameworks**: SILEX (bilingual municipal systems dataset) includes 7 work packages, deliverables, SHACL validation, and risks (legal delays, data mapping gaps). ORION creates NEXUS entity data packages; ARIADNA benchmarks retrieval with 2,302 bilingual questions (recall@10: hybrid 0.80 vs. BM25 0.69). VERDANT ENERGY standardizes energy data (installations, quality codes).  
- **Ontologies & Data Models**: SILEX v1.1 uses language-independent identifiers and bilingual labels (`PublicService`). LUMEN defines archival terms (ES/EN); SolCentro specifies energy data fields.  
- **Validation & Testing**: SILEX Mapping Report resolved 63 violations (96.4% completeness) to 4 legal issues. ARIADNA evaluates systems via recall@10, hybrid models improve multi-hop queries but increase latency. Testing includes authentication, access control, and failure classification (blocking/major/minor).  
- **Governance & Controls**: Projects require version-controlled deliverables, legal confirmations, and data minimization policies. Controls (environment separation, logging) have owners, frequency, and evidence requirements; failures exclude datasets from products.  
- **Storage/Access Control**: Immutable storage, encryption, and retention policies; restricted spaces avoid personal sync. VERDANT API enforces policy checks, authentication, and 15-minute data restrictions.  
- **Risks & Limitations**: Risks include legal delays (SILEX), translation errors (LUMEN), and unresolved entity disambiguation (94% precision). Limitations: small sample sizes, multilingual model dependence (ARIADNA), incomplete documentation, and cross-system consistency issues (e.g., conflicting section numbering).  
- **Procurement/Maintenance**: Atlas-2 storage expansion prioritized Offer B (EUR 38,450, 120 TB, 5-year warranty). Maintenance includes firmware updates and post-upgrade verification (84 TB → 196 TB).  
- **Recruitment/Onboarding**: 12-month data engineer plan requires Python/SQL/version control; onboarding includes 1-week setup across ARIADNA/LUMEN/VERDANT systems.

Claim: BM25 achieves recall@10 of 0.69, MRR of 0.52, and median latency of 74 ms.
Source content: ARIADNA RETRIEVAL BASELINE COMPARISON REPORT V1.0

1. Objective

This report compares BM25, dense retrieval, and hybrid retrieval on the corrected ARIADNA split. Earlier results obtained from a split affected by leakage are retained only for auditing and are not used to compare systems.

The main evaluation uses recall@10, MRR, latency, and analysis by category. Experiments use 256-token chunks, three seeds where applicable, and the corpus freeze date recorded in the manifest.

2. Systems

BM25 serves as the lexical baseline and uses title, tags, and text. Dense retrieval uses a multilingual model. The hybrid system combines lexical and dense scores and applies lightweight reranking. Configurations share the same document collection and version filters.

3. Overall results

BM25 achieves recall@10 of 0.69, MRR of 0.52, and median latency of 74 ms. Hybrid retrieval achieves recall@10 of 0.80, MRR of 0.63, and median latency of 182 ms. Improvement is concentrated in semantic, multi-hop, and temporal questions. BM25 retains an advantage for exact identifiers and highly specific strings.

Detailed result 1

Analysis 1: direct questions. Results show that both systems retrieve sources containing explicit terms well. Recall, rank of the first relevant result, number of required sources, and latency are compared. Errors are manually reviewed to distinguish query, index, chunking, version, or relevance defects. Comparison uses confidence intervals and retains individual runs rather than the mean alone. A small difference is not presented as a definitive conclusion.

Detailed result 2

Analysis 2: temporal questions. Results show that hybrid retrieval finds related documents better but requires validity filters. Recall, rank of the first relevant result, number of required sources, and latency are compared. Errors are manually reviewed to distinguish query, index, chunking, version, or relevance defects. Comparison uses confidence intervals and retains individual runs rather than the mean alone. A small difference is not presented as a definitive conclusion.

Detailed result 3

Analysis 3: multi-hop questions. Results show that retrieval of complementary sources improves with dense signals. Recall, rank of the first relevant result, number of required sources, and latency are compared. Errors are manually reviewed to distinguish query, index, chunking, version, or relevance defects. Comparison uses confidence intervals and retains individual runs rather than the mean alone. A small difference is not presented as a definitive conclusion.

Detailed result 4

Analysis 4: version comparison. Results show that BM25 locates version numbers while hybrid retrieval broadens context. Recall, rank of the first relevant result, number of required sources, and latency are compared. Errors are manually reviewed to distinguish query, index, chunking, version, or relevance defects. Comparison uses confidence intervals and retains individual runs rather than the mean alone. A small difference is not presented as a definitive conclusion.

Detailed result 5

Analysis 5: unanswerable questions. Results show that no retriever should be treated as a perfect detector of absence. Recall, rank of the first relevant result, number of required sources, and latency are compared. Errors are manually reviewed to distinguish query, index, chunking, version, or relevance defects. Comparison uses confidence intervals and retains individual runs rather than the mean alone. A small difference is not presented as a definitive conclusion.

Detailed result 6

Experiment 1 compares C256 versus C512. The corpus, split, questions, and evaluation remain fixed. Any additional change is recorded as a separate factor. Results contain the exact configuration, seed, chunk count, and index checksum. Final selection considers effectiveness, operating cost, explainability, and cross-language stability. A configuration is not selected from one aggregate metric alone.

Detailed result 7

gt_evidences.text: Initial validation identified forty-seven non-normalized dates, twenty-nine ambiguous senders, eighteen place names without a sufficient candidate, twelve files with checksums differing from the manifest, and nine pending rights values. The batch was processed after applying terminology guide v1.1, the approximate-date schema, and corrections arising from the first linking evaluation. The run received 1,180 letter records and 1,164 digital files. Sixteen letters had no associated image but retained authorized metadata. The system processed every record and isolated errors without silently reducing counts. 2. ranked_retrieved_results.content: LUMEN COLLECTION WORK PLAN AND GOVERNANCE V1.0 1. Purpose LUMEN develops a bilingual knowledge graph for collections held by the Regional Archive of the Centre. The project connects objects, people, places, dates, document types, events, and rights while retaining original description and uncertainty. It does not seek to replace archival systems or turn an interpretation into a definitive fact. The plan covers source selection, terminology, modeling, ingestion, disambiguation, rights, the demonstrator, evaluation, and publication. Every activity must produce verifiable evidence. A coordination conversation does not itself alter a licence, model, or object selection; the decision must be recorded and approved by the competent party. 2. Principles The Regional Archive validates meaning, context, and conditions of use. NEXUS designs transformations, software, tests, and documentation. Original data is retained alongside normalized values. A date such as “spring 1947” keeps its literal and receives an interpreted interval. A term without an exact equivalent retains its source term.

ranked_retrieved_results.content:
**Semantic Clusters Summary:**  
1. **Project Governance & Principles**: LUMEN creates a bilingual knowledge graph for the Regional Archive, connecting entities (objects, people, events) while preserving original descriptions and uncertainty. It avoids replacing archival systems or asserting definitive facts. Verifiable evidence is required for all activities, with decisions documented and approved by competent parties.  
2. **Data Handling & Inventory**: Urban photographs (2,430 images) and municipal correspondence (1,180 letters) profiles inventory files, identifiers, licenses, date ranges, and quality pre-loading. Samples include common cases, exceptions, and failed records. Processing statuses (processed, accepted, excluded) clarify absence from open products vs. technical failures.  
3. **Validation & Retention**: The Regional Archive validates meaning and use conditions. Original data is retained alongside normalized values (e.g., "spring 1947" retains literal and interpreted intervals). Collection-specific rules are tested to prevent cross-source harm.  
4. **Reference Volumes & Rules**: Each profile (urban photographs, municipal correspondence) maintains source versions, extraction dates, retention policies, and authorized products. Collection-specific rules are tested to avoid solutions valid for one source affecting others.

ranked_retrieved_results.content: The LUMEN Rights and Reuse Protocol V1.0 defines classification modes (open, internal, restricted, pending) for metadata, images, and digital objects, with specific use permissions and controls. Objects are recorded with source, rights holder, conditions, and other metadata, assessed separately for original and digital rights. The demonstrator displays objects in full, as thumbnails, metadata-only, or excluded, without implying permission from file existence. Review processes involve classification by Mateo Ruiz Serra, archival context validation by Eva Calderón Gil, and licence review by Clara Ibáñez Soto. Uncertain cases remain pending until resolved. Controls emphasize using specific contractual/legal sources over internal notes, retaining historical versions when conditions change, generating public packages from approved lists with automated checks, and managing withdrawals with identifiers, reasons, dates, and verified deletions of caches/thumbnails.

ranked_retrieved_results.content: The LUMEN Terminology Guide V1.0 establishes bilingual (English/Spanish) labels and criteria for archival terms, with each entry including source terms, preferred labels, definitions, scope, examples, provenance, and status. Identifiers are language-independent; translations are added only when they refer to the same concept. Spanish source terms are retained if no direct English equivalent exists, with functional English labels and notes. Regional Archive examples override general dictionaries for institutional usage. Personal names are untranslated; institutional names use official forms. Original titles are preserved, with access translations marked but not replacing source titles. Entries remain provisional without validated examples or Regional Archive decisions. Terms include "creator," "intellectual author," "producer," "fonds," "record series," "case file," "item," "municipal register of residents," "minute book," "official certification note," "forwarding memorandum," "public notice," "unlinked mention," and "provisional person," each defined with specific archival contexts. Notes clarify potential external interpretations.

ranked_retrieved_results.content: The LUMEN demonstrator (V1.0) enables search and exploration of Regional Archive objects via people, places, dates, and relations, with interfaces in Spanish and English that preserve query context during language switching. It includes features such as basic search, filters, result listings, object/person/place pages, relation navigation, rights presentation, and error handling, but excludes data editing and bulk download. Functional requirements specify input, output, accessibility, and testing across languages using diverse collection types. Interface states (e.g., no results, missing images, approximate dates) clarify uncertainty, avoid invented substitutes, and distinguish pending/restricted statuses. Data presentation adheres to graph and rights policies, with abbreviated labels linking to full definitions. Accessibility requirements include keyboard navigation, contrast, and alternative text. Testing prioritizes user verification over technical evaluation.

ranked_retrieved_results.content: The SILEX Mapping and Validation Report documents the transformation of a municipal catalogue into the SILEX ontology, validation of batch 3 (412 records), and criteria for accepting the candidate version. Initial validation identified 63 violations across 41 records, including missing competent units (28), non-normalized dates (17), duplicate identifiers (11), and out-of-vocabulary statuses (7). Corrections included assigning stable codes, adjusting date formats, resolving identifier collisions via compound identifiers (e.g., SM-URBAN-TERRACE-042), and revising SHACL-shape rules to exclude informational records from mandatory channel requirements. Post-correction results reduced critical violations to four pending legal bases; 96.4% of mandatory fields were complete, and bilingual label coverage reached 100%. Risks include delayed municipal confirmation of legal bases, which could delay publication. The report retains pre- and post-correction data, with annexes detailing evidence requirements, rerun procedures, manual reviews, and traceability. Final acceptance depends on municipal validation and repetition of full validation.

Claim: The final package will contain an exclusion list with reasons so that absence of a dataset is not interpreted as an ingestion failure.
Source content: The person responsible for loading will check that the received file matches the authorization record. If additional fields appear, loading will stop until their treatment is confirmed. The manifest will record the result of this check, the file checksum, and any filtering performed before storage. Pending datasets will remain separate from authorized datasets so that an automated task cannot include them in a publication.

Annex B. Pre-publication review criteria

The pre-publication review must answer five questions: whether the dataset has a sufficient licence, whether it contains only necessary fields, whether versions and validity periods are correct, whether unnecessary personal data has been removed, and whether provenance explains every value. The answers must be documented by both a technical reviewer and a person responsible for licences or privacy.

Where a record combines sources with different conditions, the most restrictive condition will apply to the combined product unless the parts can be separated verifiably. Licence errors are blocking even where the record has passed technical tests. The final package will contain an exclusion list with reasons so that absence of a dataset is not interpreted as an ingestion failure.

ranked_retrieved_results.content: ORION MIGRATION POSTMORTEM REPORT V1.0 1. Incident summary Comparison of the original export and migrated database identified forty-three potentially duplicate profile pairs. The main cause was that publication and project systems used different identifiers and linking ran before the complete identifier history was loaded. The migration also lost 126 old internal identifiers, thirty-eight affiliation end dates, seventeen software URLs, and several bilingual dataset descriptions. The export to ARIADNA stopped before these defects propagated into the corpus. 2. Impact The original source was not lost, and incorrect profiles were not published outside the internal environment. However, the migrated database was unsuitable for questions about identity, affiliation history, or relations among projects and publications. Results generated during the affected window were marked provisional. 3. Root cause The migration assumed that one local identifier was sufficient to join records. Load order omitted historical tables needed to resolve equivalences. Some rules treated missing values as ordinary gaps rather than distinguishing loss, non-applicability, and pending data.

Purpose This report documents final validation of the reusable ORION package and the technical, documentary, and administrative closure of the project. Validation checks that research profiles, affiliations, projects, publications, datasets, software, and relations can be reused without losing provenance or confusing historical records with current states. The final delivery contains normalized tables, an identity table, redirects, version relations, vocabularies, manifests, checksums, transformation rules, and exclusion documentation. Ambiguous records remain outside the reusable package and retain their exclusion reason. 2. Eight profiles remain unresolved and stay in the pending inventory. Fifteen historical records are retained as earlier states and marked through supersession relations. Final review identified zero duplicate identifiers, zero relations without a target, zero version cycles, and zero orphaned bilingual pairs.

- **Projects & Frameworks**: SILEX (bilingual municipal systems dataset) includes 7 work packages, deliverables, SHACL validation, and risks (legal delays, data mapping gaps). ORION creates NEXUS entity data packages; ARIADNA benchmarks retrieval with 2,302 bilingual questions (recall@10: hybrid 0.80 vs. BM25 0.69). VERDANT ENERGY standardizes energy data (installations, quality codes).  
- **Ontologies & Data Models**: SILEX v1.1 uses language-independent identifiers and bilingual labels (`PublicService`). LUMEN defines archival terms (ES/EN); SolCentro specifies energy data fields.  
- **Validation & Testing**: SILEX Mapping Report resolved 63 violations (96.4% completeness) to 4 legal issues. ARIADNA evaluates systems via recall@10, hybrid models improve multi-hop queries but increase latency. Testing includes authentication, access control, and failure classification (blocking/major/minor).  
- **Governance & Controls**: Projects require version-controlled deliverables, legal confirmations, and data minimization policies. Controls (environment separation, logging) have owners, frequency, and evidence requirements; failures exclude datasets from products.  
- **Storage/Access Control**: Immutable storage, encryption, and retention policies; restricted spaces avoid personal sync. VERDANT API enforces policy checks, authentication, and 15-minute data restrictions.  
- **Risks & Limitations**: Risks include legal delays (SILEX), translation errors (LUMEN), and unresolved entity disambiguation (94% precision). Limitations: small sample sizes, multilingual model dependence (ARIADNA), incomplete documentation, and cross-system consistency issues (e.g., conflicting section numbering).  
- **Procurement/Maintenance**: Atlas-2 storage expansion prioritized Offer B (EUR 38,450, 120 TB, 5-year warranty). Maintenance includes firmware updates and post-upgrade verification (84 TB → 196 TB).  
- **Recruitment/Onboarding**: 12-month data engineer plan requires Python/SQL/version control; onboarding includes 1-week setup across ARIADNA/LUMEN/VERDANT systems.

6. Validation and acceptance

Validation will combine schema checks, SHACL shapes, regression tests, and manual review. Minimum criteria are zero duplicate identifiers, zero critical errors, complete language labels, at least 95% completeness for mandatory fields, and ES/EN result equivalence of at least 98%. Accepted warnings must correspond to known exceptions.

The API must respond in less than two seconds at the 95th percentile for the agreed queries. Users will complete six tasks. A defect is considered blocking if it prevents discovery of a procedure, displays an incorrect deadline, loses context when language changes, or exposes unauthorized data.

7. Communication and change control

Formal communications will use email and remain linked to the corresponding document or decision. Chats support coordination but do not replace approval. Changes to scope, date, licence, or acceptance criteria require a request containing reason, impact, alternatives, and owners.

The current plan will remain available when a revision is published. A new version will state which sections changed and from what date they apply. History will not be rewritten to make a provisional proposal appear to have been approved from the beginning.

R1. Incomplete mappings

Fields without a responsible unit or legal basis may prevent transformation. Mitigation consists of requesting a new export, explicitly marking pending values, and not inferring information absent from an authorized source.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

R2. Duplicate identifiers

Reuse of local codes may cause collisions. Identifiers will combine the source system, procedure type, and local number, and a regression test will prevent recurrence.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

R3. Registration-data licence

Lack of formal confirmation limits scope. Registration data will remain outside the public pilot and will be used in internal tests only where written authorization exists.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

R4. Bilingual inconsistency

Divergent labels or messages may produce different results. Every class, property, status, and API message will be reviewed in parallel and use a shared language-independent identifier.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

R5. Environment delay

Unavailability of municipal infrastructure may shorten testing. An equivalent UPSC environment will be retained, but final acceptance requires repeating checks on the municipal network.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

R6. SHACL false positives

Overly general rules may flag informational procedures as errors. Shapes will be conditional on procedure type, and accepted warnings will include justification.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

Claim: The final package will contain an exclusion list with reasons so that absence of a dataset is not interpreted as an ingestion failure.
Source content: The person responsible for loading will check that the received file matches the authorization record. If additional fields appear, loading will stop until their treatment is confirmed. The manifest will record the result of this check, the file checksum, and any filtering performed before storage. Pending datasets will remain separate from authorized datasets so that an automated task cannot include them in a publication.

Annex B. Pre-publication review criteria

The pre-publication review must answer five questions: whether the dataset has a sufficient licence, whether it contains only necessary fields, whether versions and validity periods are correct, whether unnecessary personal data has been removed, and whether provenance explains every value. The answers must be documented by both a technical reviewer and a person responsible for licences or privacy.

Where a record combines sources with different conditions, the most restrictive condition will apply to the combined product unless the parts can be separated verifiably. Licence errors are blocking even where the record has passed technical tests. The final package will contain an exclusion list with reasons so that absence of a dataset is not interpreted as an ingestion failure.

Claim: A defect is considered blocking if it prevents discovery of a procedure, displays an incorrect deadline, loses context when language changes, or exposes unauthorized data.
Source content: Every load will have a manifest, checksum, date, licence, source system, and owner. Transformations will preserve the original value where normalization changes its form. Corrected errors will remain linked to the earlier version for auditing.

6. Validation and acceptance

Validation will combine schema checks, SHACL shapes, regression tests, and manual review. Minimum criteria are zero duplicate identifiers, zero critical errors, complete language labels, at least 95% completeness for mandatory fields, and ES/EN result equivalence of at least 98%. Accepted warnings must correspond to known exceptions.

The API must respond in less than two seconds at the 95th percentile for the agreed queries. Users will complete six tasks. A defect is considered blocking if it prevents discovery of a procedure, displays an incorrect deadline, loses context when language changes, or exposes unauthorized data.

7. Communication and change control

Formal communications will use email and remain linked to the corresponding document or decision. Chats support coordination but do not replace approval. Changes to scope, date, licence, or acceptance criteria require a request containing reason, impact, alternatives, and owners.

The current plan will remain available when a revision is published. A new version will state which sections changed and from what date they apply. History will not be rewritten to make a provisional proposal appear to have been approved from the beginning.

R1. Incomplete mappings

Fields without a responsible unit or legal basis may prevent transformation. Mitigation consists of requesting a new export, explicitly marking pending values, and not inferring information absent from an authorized source.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

R2. Duplicate identifiers

Reuse of local codes may cause collisions. Identifiers will combine the source system, procedure type, and local number, and a regression test will prevent recurrence.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

R3. Registration-data licence

Lack of formal confirmation limits scope. Registration data will remain outside the public pilot and will be used in internal tests only where written authorization exists.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

R4. Bilingual inconsistency

Divergent labels or messages may produce different results. Every class, property, status, and API message will be reviewed in parallel and use a shared language-independent identifier.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

R5. Environment delay

Unavailability of municipal infrastructure may shorten testing. An equivalent UPSC environment will be retained, but final acceptance requires repeating checks on the municipal network.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

R6. SHACL false positives

Overly general rules may flag informational procedures as errors. Shapes will be conditional on procedure type, and accepted warnings will include justification.

The risk will be reviewed at every steering meeting until closure. The owner will document probability, impact, action, target date, and evidence. A risk will close only when the condition has disappeared or a tested control reduces impact to the accepted level.

R7. Pilot-date change

1. Summary

ORION consolidated information about projects, publications, datasets, software, and research profiles within the NEXUS group. The final result is a reusable package with stable identifiers, verified relations, provenance, and sufficient documentation for controlled incorporation into ARIADNA and other internal systems.

The package does not reproduce every field from the original system. Internal metrics, audit records, personal addresses, review notes, and attributes without a clear purpose in the reusable product are excluded. Included fields retain their source system and extraction date.

2. Scope

The delivery contains tables for people, affiliations, projects, publications, datasets, software, organizations, and relations. It also includes identity tables, vocabularies, manifests, checksums, transformation rules, and an exclusion inventory.

Eight profiles remain outside the package because their identity could not be resolved with sufficient evidence. Fifteen historical records are retained as controlled distractors and explicitly marked as superseded versions or earlier states.

3. Principles

Reuse is based on traceability, minimization, version control, and separation between source and derived data. An inferred relation does not replace evidence. Profile merges require a recorded decision and retain earlier identifiers through equivalence relations.

questions.question: How did Atlas-2's capacity and operational status change during the September 2026 maintenance window?

gt_evidences.text: Usable capacity increased from 84 TB to 196 TB. Twelve disks, two enclosures, and an additional controller were installed. The configuration tolerates two disk failures in every group. Read, write, simulated-failure, and restoration tests completed successfully.
Service became available again on 13 September at 18:10. Two research jobs resumed from checkpoints, and one was rerun. No project information was lost.

ranked_retrieved_results.content: ATLAS-2 MAINTENANCE AND CAPACITY UPGRADE REPORT V1.0 1. Summary The Atlas-2 maintenance window took place on 12 and 13 September 2026. It included storage expansion, updates to the base system, GPU drivers, the queue service, monitoring, and backup verification. Usable capacity increased from 84 TB to 196 TB. Twelve disks, two enclosures, and an additional controller were installed. The configuration tolerates two disk failures in every group. Read, write, simulated-failure, and restoration tests completed successfully. Service became available again on 13 September at 18:10. Two research jobs resumed from checkpoints, and one was rerun. No project information was lost. 2. Scope The intervention covered CPU nodes, three GPUs, working storage, archive storage, authentication, queues, monitoring, and backups. Access groups and quotas were not changed without a specific request. 3. Preparation Before the window, users were notified, new submissions stopped, backups verified, and active jobs recorded.

ranked_retrieved_results.content: ATLAS-2 OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE MANUAL V1.2 1. Purpose Atlas-2 is the shared computing and storage infrastructure of the NEXUS group. This manual defines daily operation, accounts, queues, storage, backups, maintenance, updates, monitoring, incidents, and recovery. The purpose is to provide reproducible capacity without compromising other projects or restricted data. The manual distinguishes administration, research use, and support. Users do not receive administrative permissions by default. Jobs must be identified, use persistent paths, and record the configuration required to reproduce results. 2. Components Atlas-2 includes CPU nodes, three GPUs, working storage, archival storage, a queue service, authentication, monitoring, and backups. Every component has an owner, version, dependencies, health check, and restoration procedure. 3. Principles Operation follows least privilege, project separation, quotas, traceability, and planned maintenance. Temporary jobs do not replace the archive. Restricted data is stored in separate directories with specific groups.

ranked_retrieved_results.content: ATLAS-2 STORAGE EXPANSION PROCUREMENT DECISION V1.0 Purpose This document records the comparison and purchasing decision for expansion of Atlas-2 storage. The need results from growth in ARIADNA corpora, LUMEN images, VERDANT products, and project working copies. Requirements The solution must provide at least 120 TB of usable capacity, tolerance of two disk failures, compatibility with the current system, monitoring, a five-year warranty, and delivery before 31 August 2026. The purchase includes disks, enclosures, controller, installation, and testing. Offers Three comparable offers were received. Offer A has the lowest price but only a three-year warranty. Offer B meets every requirement and includes installation and a recovery test. Offer C provides greater capacity but exceeds the available budget and has an incompatible delivery date. Decision Offer B is selected for EUR 38,450, taxes included. The decision is not based on price alone: it includes warranty, compatibility, support, delivery, and restoration evidence.

Objective SILEX demonstrates that a heterogeneous municipal catalogue can be transformed into an interoperable, bilingual, and verifiable semantic representation. The pilot covers the catalogue, ontology, mappings, API, deployment, training, evaluation with municipal staff, transfer, and closure. Version 1.1 strengthens the distinction between proposal and approval. Dates, requirements, and exceptions must retain their status. A coordination conversation may produce a proposal, but the plan changes only where a formal recorded decision exists.

Source content: Every case was assigned an owner and target date. The correction must preserve evidence of the previous value and run through the pipeline. Where a correction changes meaning, review by the municipal owner is required.

5. Duplicate-identifier incident

Identifier SM-LIC-042 was used for both a terrace and a market stall because two municipal applications shared numbering. Loading stopped before resources were overwritten. The solution combines system, domain, and local number: SM-URBAN-TERRACE-042 and SM-MARKET-STALL-042.

The regression test searches for repetition within the batch, across previous loads, and among different types. It also verifies that references to documents and units are updated with the new identifier. The old source code is retained as an alternative identifier with provenance.

6. SHACL-shape adjustments

The channel shape required at least one value for every record. This was incorrect for purely informational records. The new rule applies cardinality only to procedures that accept an application or provide an operational service. Informational records may declare the field non-applicable.

The date rule is extended to accept a year, interval, or exact date but not free text without an assessment. Bilingual labels are checked by base identifier. The version shape prevents cycles and requires reciprocity between previous and next versions.

7. Regression set

The set contains twenty-four procedures not used during diagnosis: six permits, five certificates, four grants, four prior notifications, and five informational records. It checks the identifier, unit, legal basis, channel, deadline, status, and labels.

It contains two non-applicable cases and three pending fields to prevent corrections from turning explicit states into gaps. The expected result is zero duplicates and zero labels without a language. A recurring failure blocks publication of ontology v1.2.

8. Post-correction results

The second run reduced critical violations to four records with legal bases awaiting municipal validation. These cases will not be published as complete and will retain the pending assessment. Duplicates, date formats, and unmapped statuses were corrected.

The nine channel warnings disappeared after the rule became conditional. Comparison of reports confirms that no correction removed original information. ES/EN label coverage reached 100% in the batch, and completeness of publishable mandatory fields was 96.4%.

9. Risks and schedule

Validation depends on Santa Marina confirming the four pending legal bases. Schedule risk remains open: if confirmation arrives after August, the final load and pilot must be rescheduled. An alternative date will not be treated as approved until formal communication is received.

The deliverable must clearly distinguish the plan date from a change proposal. Metrics, annexes, and examples will be reviewed in both the editable source and PDF. Required signatures are those of Javier Ortega Campos and Luis Noguera.

10. Conclusions

The approach transforms the catalogue without hiding uncertainty. Separating missing, non-applicable, excluded, and pending values was essential to avoid false errors and complete the model without inventing data. Compound identifiers remove collisions, and regression tests reduce the risk of recurrence.

The candidate version may proceed to pre-production once municipal confirmations are incorporated, full validation is repeated, and the signed report is archived. Registration data remains outside the publishable scope until a sufficient formal licence exists.

Annex A. Minimum evidence per record

Every publishable record must include an identified source, extraction date, licence, owner, validation result, and relation to its previous version where applicable. Transformed values must retain the source field. Isolated manual corrections are not accepted.

Annex B. Rerun procedure

The rerun starts from a clean copy, installs the exact ontology and shape versions, loads the manifest, transforms the records, executes the rules, and generates two outputs: a readable report and a structured file. Checksums are compared before approval.

Annex C. Manual-review matrix

Claim: The final package will contain an exclusion list with reasons so that absence of a dataset is not interpreted as an ingestion failure.
Source content: The person responsible for loading will check that the received file matches the authorization record. If additional fields appear, loading will stop until their treatment is confirmed. The manifest will record the result of this check, the file checksum, and any filtering performed before storage. Pending datasets will remain separate from authorized datasets so that an automated task cannot include them in a publication.

Annex B. Pre-publication review criteria

The pre-publication review must answer five questions: whether the dataset has a sufficient licence, whether it contains only necessary fields, whether versions and validity periods are correct, whether unnecessary personal data has been removed, and whether provenance explains every value. The answers must be documented by both a technical reviewer and a person responsible for licences or privacy.

Where a record combines sources with different conditions, the most restrictive condition will apply to the combined product unless the parts can be separated verifiably. Licence errors are blocking even where the record has passed technical tests. The final package will contain an exclusion list with reasons so that absence of a dataset is not interpreted as an ingestion failure.
